C-style struct representing a numeric sequence for indexing. Fields: begin (start), end (inclusive stop), and step (increment). Used throughout ArrayFire for slicing/indexing and for constructing af::seq in C++ APIs. Static constant af_span and C API helper af_make_seq use this type.

C++ class wrapper around af_seq for building index sequences for af::array. Stores the underlying C struct (s), a cached size, and a gfor flag. Provides constructors from length, explicit begin/end/step, another seq with gfor flag, and from af_seq; arithmetic operators to offset/scale/negate sequences; and implicit conversion to af::array producing the explicit values. Lifetime managed by C++; no special destruction beyond ~seq(). Details of init and size computation are not exposed here.

Four-dimensional size/shape utility class in namespace af. Stores up to four dim_t dimensions and provides element-wise arithmetic, indexing, element counts, and stream I/O helpers. Used to represent array extents in ArrayFire. Details about dim_t come from included headers and are not defined here.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for float. Provides ArrayFire enum type IDs for single-precision reals, exposes base_type as float, and a human-readable name.
Specializations of af::dtype_traits for single-precision complex numbers. Both af::cfloat and std::complex<float> map to ArrayFire complex32 type; base_type is float.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for double-precision reals. Maps to ArrayFire f64; base_type is double.
Specializations of af::dtype_traits for double-precision complex numbers. Both af::cdouble and std::complex<double> map to ArrayFire complex64; base_type is double.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for char, mapping to ArrayFire boolean-8 (b8). Base type is char.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 32-bit signed integers. Maps to s32; base_type is int.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 32-bit unsigned integers. Maps to u32; base_type is unsigned.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 8-bit unsigned integers (byte). Maps to u8; base_type is unsigned char.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 64-bit signed integers. Maps to s64; base_type is long long.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 64-bit unsigned integers. Maps to u64; base_type is unsigned long long.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 16-bit signed integers (available when AF_API_VERSION >= 32). Maps to s16; base_type is short.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 16-bit unsigned integers (available when AF_API_VERSION >= 32). Maps to u16; base_type is unsigned short.
Specialization of af::dtype_traits for 8-bit signed integers when AF_API_VERSION >= 310. Maps to s8; base_type is signed char.

C++ high-level N-dimensional GPU/CPU array container for ArrayFire. Manages an underlying af_array handle with copy-on-write semantics, rich construction from sizes or host/device pointers, indexing through array_proxy, type/dimension queries, evaluation control, device pointer access, and many arithmetic and logical operator overloads.

Internal proxy type returned by af::array indexing operations. Represents a view/slice of a parent array and supports assignment and most af::array query/utility methods. Not intended for direct user instantiation outside indexing flows.

objects.description: Opaque C handle to an ArrayFire event object. It is a pointer-sized token managed by the ArrayFire runtime; the concrete pointee type is intentionally hidden. Use the provided C API to create, mark, wait/enqueue, block, and delete it. Do not dereference or free directly; always destroy with af_delete_event.

C++ RAII wrapper around af_event. Manages lifetime and provides member functions to mark the event on the default queue, enqueue a wait on the active queue, and block the calling thread. Copy is disabled; move is supported when AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled. Destructor releases the underlying af_event (implementation not shown here but implied by RAII).

ArrayFire exception class in namespace af. Wraps an af_err code and a fixed-size message buffer, derives from std::exception and provides what() plus several constructors to format error messages. Used to report ArrayFire errors to C++ callers.

objects.definition: typedef void* af_memory_manager;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an ArrayFire memory manager instance. It represents a user-implementable memory manager object whose behavior is defined by attaching callback function pointers via the provided setter APIs. The handle itself is a void* and should be treated as opaque by users; ArrayFire will pass it back into callbacks. Lifetime is managed via af_create_memory_manager/af_release_memory_manager and selection via af_set_memory_manager/af_unset_memory_manager (and their pinned equivalents).

objects.definition: typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_initialize_fn)(af_memory_manager handle);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked after a memory manager is set and becomes active. Intended for any initialization required by the custom memory manager.

objects.definition: typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_shutdown_fn)(af_memory_manager handle);
objects.description: Function pointer type for a callback invoked when a memory manager is unset and becomes unused. Should release resources owned by the custom manager as appropriate.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_alloc_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                             void** ptr,
                                             /* bool */ int user_lock,
                                             const unsigned ndims, dim_t* dims,
                                             const unsigned element_size);
objects.description: Function pointer type for allocating a buffer. Must allocate a buffer of dims (elements) × element_size bytes and return it via ptr. If user_lock is truthy, associate a user lock with the allocation. ndims is currently always 1. Implementations may modify dims to reflect the resulting shape.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_allocated_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                                 size_t* size, void* ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type to query the allocated size, in bytes, of a given pointer managed by the memory manager.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_unlock_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                              void* ptr, /* bool */ int user_unlock);
objects.description: Function pointer type to unlock a buffer from use. If user_unlock is truthy, also remove the user lock and potentially free if eligible.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_signal_memory_cleanup_fn)(
    af_memory_manager handle);
objects.description: Function pointer type called to signal that the memory manager should attempt to free memory if possible (e.g., after OOM from external allocations).

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_print_info_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                                  char* buffer, int id);
objects.description: Function pointer type to populate a human-readable summary of the manager’s current state for the given device id into the provided character buffer.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_user_lock_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                                 void* ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type to mark a buffer as user-owned (user locked) to prevent internal reclamation.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_user_unlock_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                                   void* ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type to remove the user-owned (user lock) state from a buffer.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_is_user_locked_fn)(af_memory_manager handle,
                                                      int* out, void* ptr);
objects.description: Function pointer type to query whether a buffer is user locked. Writes a truthy value to out if it is.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_get_memory_pressure_fn)(
    af_memory_manager handle, float* pressure);
objects.description: Function pointer type to return a memory pressure metric (implementation-defined) via pressure, used by the JIT to decide evaluation.

objects.definition:
typedef af_err (*af_memory_manager_jit_tree_exceeds_memory_pressure_fn)(
    af_memory_manager handle, int* out, size_t size);
objects.description: Function pointer type consulted by the JIT to determine if the bytes referenced by the current JIT tree (size) exert too much memory pressure. Writes truthy to out if pressure is too high.

objects.definition:

functions.name: af::seq::seq

functions.name: af::constant

template<typename T>
array constant(T val, const dim4 &dims, const dtype ty=(af_dtype)dtype_traits<T>::ctype);
functions.description: Creates an ArrayFire array whose elements are set to the specified constant value. This overload takes a dim4 shape. Use when you know the full shape as a dim4 and optionally want to control the array dtype.
requirements: dims specifies the desired array shape; each component represents the size of a dimension.
ty specifies the output dtype; by default it is inferred from T via dtype_traits.
T must be convertible to the requested dtype ty.
Caller must include ArrayFire headers and use within C++ with namespace af.
No explicit constraints on dimension sizes are documented; typical usage implies non-negative sizes.

functions.signature: AFAPI array identity(const dim4 &dims, const dtype ty=f32);
functions.description: Generates an identity array (ones on the main diagonal, zeros elsewhere) of the given shape and type.
requirements: dims specifies the output shape; for identity behavior, only the first two dimensions are relevant for the diagonal.
ty specifies the output dtype; defaults to f32.

functions.name: af::range
functions.signature: AFAPI array range(const dim4 &dims, const int seq_dim = -1, const dtype ty=f32);
functions.description: Generates an array containing sequences [0, n-1] along seq_dim tiled across other dimensions per dims. Use -1 to default to the last dimension or library-defined behavior.
requirements: dims specifies output shape.
seq_dim selects the dimension along which the ramp increases; default -1 uses a library-defined dimension (commonly the first or last).
ty specifies the output dtype; defaults to f32.

functions.name: af::iota
functions.signature: AFAPI array iota(const dim4 &dims, const dim4 &tile_dims = dim4(1), const dtype ty=f32);
functions.description: Generates an array containing values 0..(prod(dims)-1) (conceptually), reshaped to dims and tiled per tile_dims. Use to create index-like grids.
requirements: dims specifies the base shape.
tile_dims specifies how many times to tile along each dimension; defaults to 1 in all dims.
ty specifies the output dtype; defaults to f32.

requirements: in must be a valid af::array.
num selects which diagonal: 0 is the main, positive for superdiagonals, negative for subdiagonals.

functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_range(af_array *out, const unsigned ndims, const dim_t * const dims, const int seq_dim, const af_dtype type);

functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_diag_create(af_array *out, const af_array in, const int num);

in must be a valid array interpreted as a diagonal vector.
num selects which diagonal to populate (0 main, positive upper, negative lower).

functions.name: af_diag_extract
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_diag_extract(af_array *out, const af_array in, const int num);

in must be a valid array.
num selects which diagonal to extract.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

first and second must be valid arrays with matching sizes in non-concatenated dimensions and compatible types.
dim chooses the concatenation dimension.

functions.name: af_join_many
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_join_many(af_array *out, const int dim, const unsigned n_arrays, const af_array *inputs);
functions.description: C API: Concatenates up to 10 arrays along dimension dim. Empty arrays are ignored.

functions.name: af_tile
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_tile(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned x, const unsigned y, const unsigned z, const unsigned w);
functions.description: C API: Tiles the input array by repeating it x, y, z, w times along each dimension. Counts include the original.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
x, y, z, w specify repeat counts including the original copy.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_reorder
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_reorder(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned x, const unsigned y, const unsigned z, const unsigned w);
functions.description: C API: Reorders the dimensions of in so that dimension indices x, y, z, w become the new order.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
x, y, z, w are dimension indices defining a permutation.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_shift
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_shift(af_array *out, const af_array in, const int x, const int y, const int z, const int w);

requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
x, y, z, w specify integer shifts for each dimension.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_moddims
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_moddims(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned ndims, const dim_t * const dims);
functions.description: C API: Reshapes the input array to the provided dimensions without changing data.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
ndims must match the length of dims; dims must point to ndims entries.
Product of dims must equal the number of elements in in (implied by reshape semantics).
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_flat
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_flat(af_array *out, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Flattens the input array into a 1-D array.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_flip
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_flip(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned dim);
functions.description: C API: Flips the input array along the specified dimension.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
dim selects the axis to flip.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_lower
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_lower(af_array *out, const af_array in, bool is_unit_diag);
functions.description: C API: Returns the lower triangle of in, optionally forcing the diagonal to 1.

in must be a valid array.

functions.name: af_upper
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_upper(af_array *out, const af_array in, bool is_unit_diag);
functions.description: C API: Returns the upper triangle of in, optionally forcing the diagonal to 1.
requirements: out must be a valid output pointer.
in must be a valid array.
If is_unit_diag is true, diagonal elements are set to 1 in the result.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_select
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const af_array a, const af_array b);
functions.description: C API: Selects elements from a or b based on cond: out = cond ? a : b elementwise.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid output pointer.
cond must be a conditional array (boolean-like).
a and b must be valid arrays, conformable in shape and type-compatible.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_select_scalar_r
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select_scalar_r(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const af_array a, const double b);
functions.description: C API: Selects elements from array a or scalar b based on cond (right scalar version): out = cond ? a : b.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid output pointer.
cond must be a conditional array (boolean-like).
a must be a valid array; b is a scalar convertible to a's dtype.
Shapes of cond and a must be conformable.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_select_scalar_l
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select_scalar_l(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const double a, const af_array b);
functions.description: C API: Selects elements from scalar a or array b based on cond (left scalar version): out = cond ? a : b.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid output pointer.
cond must be a conditional array (boolean-like).
b must be a valid array; a is a scalar convertible to b's dtype.

Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.description: C API: In-place replacement: where cond is false, replaces elements of a with corresponding elements from b.

a and b must be valid arrays of the same shape and type-compatible.

Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_replace_scalar
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_replace_scalar(af_array a, const af_array cond, const double b);
functions.description: C API: In-place replacement with scalar: where cond is false, sets elements of a to scalar b.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
a must be a valid array; b must be convertible to a's dtype.
cond must be a conditional array conformable with a.
Mutates a in place.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_pad
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_pad(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned begin_ndims, const dim_t *const begin_dims, const unsigned end_ndims, const dim_t *const end_dims, const af_border_type pad_fill_type);

functions.name: af_select_scalar_r_long
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select_scalar_r_long(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const af_array a, const long long b);
functions.description: C API: Selects elements from array a or scalar b (long long) based on cond (right scalar version).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 39.

Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_select_scalar_r_ulong
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select_scalar_r_ulong(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const af_array a, const unsigned long long b);
functions.description: C API: Selects elements from array a or scalar b (unsigned long long) based on cond (right scalar version).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 39.

Shapes of cond and a must be conformable.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_select_scalar_l_long
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_select_scalar_l_long(af_array *out, const af_array cond, const long long a, const af_array b);

requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 39.

functions.name: af::info

functions.name: af::infoString

requirements: Caller must provide valid, writable character buffers for d_name, d_platform, d_toolkit, and d_compute with sufficient capacity; required sizes are unknown in this header.

functions.name: af::getDeviceCount

functions.name: af::getDevice

functions.description: Returns true if the specified device supports double-precision floating point operations.
requirements: device must identify a device to query; valid range is not specified here.
Function only queries capability; does not change device state.

functions.name: af::isHalfAvailable
functions.signature: AFAPI bool af::isHalfAvailable(const int device);
functions.description: Returns true if the specified device supports half-precision floating point operations.
requirements: device must identify a device to query; valid range is not specified here.
Function only queries capability; does not change device state.

functions.name: af::setDevice

May affect subsequent allocations and computations.

functions.name: af::alloc
functions.signature: AFAPI void* af::alloc(const size_t elements, const dtype type);
functions.description: Allocates device memory using ArrayFire's memory manager for the given number of elements of the specified dtype. Deprecated in favor of allocV2.
requirements: elements specifies element count; total bytes = elements * sizeof(type).
Memory must be freed using af::free() explicitly; otherwise memory is not returned to the manager.
Deprecated: prefer af::allocV2(bytes).
Only valid on the current device.

functions.name: af::allocV2
functions.signature: AFAPI void* af::allocV2(const size_t bytes);
functions.description: Allocates device memory using ArrayFire's memory manager for the given number of bytes. For OpenCL backend returns a cl_mem pointer; CUDA returns a device pointer; CPU returns a host pointer.
requirements: bytes is the number of bytes to allocate.
Memory must be freed using af::freeV2() explicitly.
Only valid on the current device.

functions.name: af::free
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::free(const void* ptr);
functions.description: Frees device memory previously allocated by af::alloc (or its templated form) and returns it to ArrayFire's memory manager. Deprecated in favor of freeV2.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by af::alloc for the active backend.
Will free a device pointer even if previously locked.
Deprecated: prefer af::freeV2 for memory from af::allocV2.

functions.name: af::freeV2
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::freeV2(const void* ptr);
functions.description: Frees device memory previously allocated by af::allocV2 and returns it to ArrayFire's memory manager. Works even if the pointer was previously locked.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by af::allocV2 for the active backend.

functions.name: af::pinned
functions.signature: AFAPI void* af::pinned(const size_t elements, const dtype type);
functions.description: Allocates pinned (page-locked) host memory for the given element count and dtype using ArrayFire's allocator.
requirements: elements specifies element count; required total bytes = elements * sizeof(type).
Caller must free the memory using af::freePinned().

functions.name: af::freePinned
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::freePinned(const void* ptr);
functions.description: Frees pinned host memory previously allocated by af::pinned and returns it to ArrayFire's allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by af::pinned.

functions.name: af::allocHost
functions.signature: AFAPI void* af::allocHost(const size_t elements, const dtype type);
functions.description: Allocates regular host memory using ArrayFire for the given element count and dtype.
requirements: elements specifies element count; total bytes = elements * sizeof(type).
Caller must free the memory using af::freeHost().

functions.name: af::freeHost
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::freeHost(const void* ptr);
functions.description: Frees host memory previously allocated by af::allocHost and returns it to ArrayFire.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by af::allocHost.

functions.description: C API: Frees host memory previously allocated by af_alloc_host.

functions.name: af_device_array
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_device_array(af_array* arr, void* data, const unsigned ndims, const dim_t* const dims, const af_dtype type);
functions.description: C API: Creates an ArrayFire array that wraps existing device memory pointer data with the specified dimensions and type.
requirements: arr must be a valid, writable pointer to receive the created array handle.
data must be a valid device pointer appropriate for the active backend; ownership and lifetime requirements are not specified here.
ndims and dims specify array shape; dims must point to at least ndims elements.
type must be a valid af_dtype matching the memory at data.

functions.name: af_device_mem_info
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_device_mem_info(size_t* alloc_bytes, size_t* alloc_buffers, size_t* lock_bytes, size_t* lock_buffers);
functions.description: C API: Retrieves memory manager statistics: total allocated bytes/buffers and currently locked bytes/buffers.
requirements: alloc_bytes, alloc_buffers, lock_bytes, and lock_buffers must be valid, writable pointers.
May perform device synchronization.

functions.name: af_print_mem_info
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_print_mem_info(const char* msg, const int device_id);
functions.description: C API: Prints a formatted table of ArrayFire Device Manager buffers. Optionally prefixes output with msg and can target a specific device ID or -1 for the active device. Performs synchronization.
requirements: If device_id != -1, it should identify a device; exact range unspecified.
Function prints to standard output and may synchronize.

functions.name: af_device_gc
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_device_gc();
functions.description: C API: Calls the garbage collection routine in the device memory manager.
requirements: No arguments. Returns af_err status.

functions.name: af_set_mem_step_size
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_set_mem_step_size(const size_t step_bytes);
functions.description: C API: Sets the minimum memory chunk size (step) for the default memory manager. Returns an error if a custom memory manager is set.
requirements: Only works with the default memory manager; will return an error with a custom manager.
step_bytes is the desired step size in bytes; valid range unspecified.

functions.name: af_get_mem_step_size
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_get_mem_step_size(size_t* step_bytes);
functions.description: C API: Gets the minimum memory chunk size (step) for the default memory manager. Returns an error if a custom memory manager is set.
requirements: step_bytes must be a valid, writable pointer.
Only works with the default memory manager; will return an error with a custom manager.

functions.name: af_lock_device_ptr
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_lock_device_ptr(const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API (deprecated in newer API versions): Locks the device buffer in the memory manager so it is not freed until unlocked.
requirements: arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle.
Caller must later unlock to allow the memory manager to reclaim the buffer.

functions.name: af_unlock_device_ptr
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_unlock_device_ptr(const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API (deprecated in newer API versions): Unlocks a device buffer previously locked, returning control to the memory manager.
requirements: arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle previously locked.

functions.name: af_lock_array
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_lock_array(const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API: Locks the device buffer in the memory manager so it is not freed until af_unlock_array is called.
requirements: arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle.
Caller must call af_unlock_array to release the lock.

functions.name: af_unlock_array
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_unlock_array(const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API: Unlocks a device buffer previously locked by af_lock_array or related APIs, returning control to the memory manager.
requirements: arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle previously locked.

functions.name: af_is_locked_array
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_is_locked_array(bool* res, const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API: Queries whether the array has been locked by the user via af_lock_array, af_get_device_ptr, or af_get_raw_ptr.
requirements: res must be a valid, writable pointer.
arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle.

functions.name: af_get_device_ptr
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_get_device_ptr(void** ptr, const af_array arr);
functions.description: C API: Retrieves the underlying device pointer for the array and locks the buffer in the memory manager. For OpenCL, *ptr should be cast to cl_mem. The buffer remains locked until explicitly unlocked.
requirements: ptr must be a valid pointer to receive the device pointer.
arr must be a valid ArrayFire array handle.
Caller must unlock the buffer afterwards (e.g., via af_unlock_device_ptr or af_unlock_array, per API version).

functions.name: af_set_kernel_cache_directory
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_set_kernel_cache_directory(const char* path, int override_env);
functions.description: C API: Sets the directory where JIT-generated kernels are cached. Can be configured to override the AF_JIT_KERNEL_CACHE_DIRECTORY environment variable.
requirements: path must not be NULL for success; AF_ERR_ARG is returned if path is NULL.
override_env determines precedence: nonzero to override environment variable, zero to let environment variable take precedence.

functions.name: af_get_kernel_cache_directory
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_get_kernel_cache_directory(size_t* length, char* path);
functions.description: C API: Gets the current JIT kernel cache directory. If path is NULL, the required length is returned via length. If both are provided, writes the path into the provided buffer.
requirements: length receives the length if path is NULL; must be a valid pointer when used that way.
If both path and length are NULL, returns AF_ERR_ARG.
If provided buffer is too small, returns AF_ERR_SIZE.
path must point to writable storage of at least *length bytes when used to receive the path.

functions.name: af::event::event
functions.signature: af::event::event(af_event e)
functions.description: Constructs an ArrayFire C++ event wrapper from an existing C af_event handle. Use this when you already have a valid C event handle and want RAII semantics in C++. Details about ownership transfer are not explicitly stated; typically the wrapper will manage the lifetime of the handle until destruction.
requirements: e must be a valid af_event handle obtained from ArrayFire (e.g., via af_create_event or returned by other ArrayFire APIs).
The handle must not be invalid or already deleted.

Behavior regarding ownership (whether the constructor assumes ownership of e) is not explicitly documented; callers should ensure the handle remains valid for the lifetime of the wrapper or consult library docs.

functions.name: af::event::event
functions.signature: af::event::event(af::event&& other)
functions.description: Move constructor for the ArrayFire event RAII class. Constructs a new event by taking ownership of the resources from another event object.
requirements: other must be an rvalue (temporary or std::move) and may not be used to manage the same underlying event after the move, per C++ move semantics.
Available only when AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled in the build environment.
The source and destination must refer to either distinct objects or a self-move-safe implementation; self-move behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: af::event::event
functions.signature: af::event::event()
functions.description: Default constructor that creates a new event object. The newly constructed event can be marked, enqueued, or blocked on via member functions.
requirements: Construction must succeed internally; no parameters required.
Subsequent member calls (mark/enqueue/block) require that the object has not been destroyed.

functions.name: af::event::operator=
functions.signature: af::event& af::event::operator=(af::event&& other)
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers ownership of the underlying af_event from other into this, releasing any currently held event in this object first.
requirements: other must be an rvalue (temporary or std::move).
After assignment, other should not be used to manage the previously held event (standard C++ move semantics).
Available only when AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled in the build environment.

functions.name: af::event::~event
functions.signature: af::event::~event()
functions.description: Destructor for the RAII event wrapper. Releases the underlying af_event handle and any associated resources.
requirements: Must not be called explicitly except by C++ object lifetime rules; do not use the object after destruction.
All outstanding operations referring to the underlying event should be in a state compatible with destruction (standard RAII assumption; specific guarantees are not documented here).

functions.name: af::event::get
functions.signature: af_event af::event::get() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying C af_event handle managed by this C++ wrapper. Useful for interoperability with the C API.
requirements: The event object must be valid (constructed and not yet destroyed).
The returned handle must be treated according to ArrayFire C API rules; do not delete it separately if the C++ object still manages it (ownership semantics are not explicitly stated here).

functions.name: af::event::mark
functions.signature: void af::event::mark()
functions.description: Adds/marks the event on the default ArrayFire queue. After the program reaches this call, the event is considered complete relative to operations already enqueued on that queue at the time of marking.
requirements: The event object must refer to a valid, initialized event (constructed and not destroyed).
A default ArrayFire computation queue must be active in the current context.

functions.name: af::event::enqueue
functions.signature: void af::event::enqueue()
functions.description: Enqueues the event on the active ArrayFire stream, so that subsequent operations will wait until the operations present when mark was called are complete.
requirements: The event object must refer to a valid, initialized event (constructed and not destroyed).
An active ArrayFire computation stream must exist in the current context.

functions.name: af::event::block
functions.signature: void af::event::block() const
functions.description: Blocks the calling thread until this event has occurred, i.e., until all operations on the computation stream that were pending at the time of mark are complete.
requirements: The event object must refer to a valid, initialized event (constructed and not destroyed).
Blocking will stall the calling thread; callers must avoid deadlocks and call from an appropriate thread/context.

functions.name: af_create_event
functions.signature: af_err af_create_event(af_event* eventHandle)
functions.description: Creates a new af_event handle. On success, writes the newly created event handle to eventHandle.
requirements: eventHandle must be a non-null pointer to an af_event variable where the created handle will be stored.
The caller is responsible for eventually releasing the created handle via af_delete_event.
Check the returned af_err for success or failure before using the output handle.

functions.name: af_delete_event
functions.signature: af_err af_delete_event(af_event eventHandle)
functions.description: Releases the af_event handle and its associated resources.
requirements: eventHandle must be a valid af_event previously created by af_create_event or otherwise obtained from ArrayFire.
Do not use eventHandle after successful deletion.
The caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_mark_event
functions.signature: af_err af_mark_event(const af_event eventHandle)
functions.description: Marks the event on the active computation stream. Any operations currently enqueued on that stream will be completed before any operations enqueued after a subsequent enqueue/wait call associated with this event.
requirements: eventHandle must be a valid af_event.
There must be an active computation stream in the current context.
The caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_enqueue_wait_event
functions.signature: af_err af_enqueue_wait_event(const af_event eventHandle)
functions.description: Enqueues the event on the active stream so that all operations submitted after this call will not execute until operations that were on the stream when mark was called are complete.
requirements: eventHandle must be a valid af_event.
There must be an active computation stream in the current context.
The caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_block_event
functions.signature: af_err af_block_event(const af_event eventHandle)
functions.description: Blocks the calling thread until all events on the computation stream prior to the corresponding mark are complete.
requirements: eventHandle must be a valid af_event.
Blocking will stall the calling thread; avoid calling from time-sensitive or deadlock-prone contexts.
The caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af::exception::err
functions.signature: af_err af::exception::err();
functions.description: Returns the error code stored in this ArrayFire exception instance. Typical usage is to catch af::exception and query the underlying af_err code for programmatic handling.
requirements: The af::exception object must be properly constructed before calling err().
No additional preconditions or side effects are specified.

functions.name: af::exception::exception
functions.signature: af::exception::exception();
functions.description: Default constructor for af::exception. Creates an exception object with an unspecified message and error code context. Details of the default state are not documented in this header.
requirements: No arguments required.
Behavior and initial error code/message are not documented here; treat as unknown.

functions.name: af::exception::what
functions.signature: const char *af::exception::what() const throw();
functions.description: Returns the exception’s human-readable message as a C string. Suitable for logging or display and used by operator<<. Declared not to throw.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the exception object is alive; do not free it.
No additional preconditions are documented.

functions.name: operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream &af::operator<<(std::ostream &s, const af::exception &e);
functions.description: Stream insertion operator for af::exception. Writes e.what() to the provided output stream and returns the stream, enabling chaining.
requirements: s must be a valid std::ostream reference.
e must be a valid af::exception reference.
The function does not modify e and is expected not to throw beyond stream failures.

functions.name: af_get_last_error
functions.signature: void af_get_last_error(char **msg, dim_t *len);
functions.description: Retrieves the last error message that occurred in the ArrayFire C API and its length. On success, writes a pointer to the message into msg and the character count into len. Intended for post-error diagnostics.
requirements: msg must be a non-null pointer to a char* variable where the function can store the address of the message buffer.
len must be a non-null pointer to a dim_t variable where the function can store the message length.
Ownership/lifetime and deallocation of the returned message buffer are not specified in this header; consult ArrayFire C API docs for required free routine (unknown here).
Thread-safety and whether the last error is cleared by this call are not specified.

functions.name: af_err_to_string
functions.signature: const char *af_err_to_string(const af_err err);
functions.description: Converts an ArrayFire error code (af_err) to its string representation. Useful for logging or displaying error information in the C API.
requirements: err should be a valid af_err enumeration value.
The returned pointer refers to a constant, read-only string; do not modify or free it.
Lifetime of the returned string is not specified here but is typically static; treat as unknown if not documented.

functions.name: af::features::features
functions.signature: af::features::features()
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates a new features handle with zero features. Use the accessor methods (getX, getY, etc.) to retrieve empty arrays until populated by feature detection routines. Details of underlying allocation are library-internal.
requirements: May only be used in C++ when including the ArrayFire C++ API (namespace af).
Resulting object must be considered valid/initialized before use; no additional setup required.
Returned object initially contains zero features; accessor arrays will be empty unless populated by other API calls.

functions.name: af::features::features
functions.signature: af::features::features(size_t n)
functions.description: Allocates a features object sized to hold n features with undefined locations/scores/orientations. Intended to pre-size a features container prior to population by detection/assignment routines.
requirements: n is the number of features to reserve/represent; values are unspecified in the arrays until written by the library or the user.
Behavior for extremely large n depends on available memory; allocation failures may throw/propagate errors.
Object is valid/initialized after construction.

functions.name: af::features::features
functions.signature: af::features::features(af_features f)
functions.description: Wraps an existing C API af_features handle in a C++ af::features object. Use when interoperating between the C and C++ APIs.
requirements: f must be a valid af_features handle obtained from the ArrayFire C API and not yet released.
Ownership/refcount semantics follow the library implementation; callers must avoid double release (do not call af_release_features on f while also letting the wrapper manage it).
The wrapped handle must remain valid for the lifetime of this af::features object.

functions.name: af::features::features
functions.signature: af::features::features(const af::features &other)
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new features object as a copy of another, typically sharing or duplicating underlying storage per ArrayFire refcount semantics.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 38.
other must be a valid, initialized af::features object.
Copies respect the library’s reference counting; both objects may share underlying arrays.

functions.name: af::features::features
functions.signature: af::features::features(af::features &&other)
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of the underlying af_features handle from other to this object, leaving other in a valid but unspecified state.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 38 and AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled.
other must be a valid, initialized af::features rvalue.
After the move, do not use other except for destruction or re-assignment.

functions.name: af::features::~features
functions.signature: af::features::~features()
functions.description: Destructor. Releases the underlying af_features handle and its associated arrays per ArrayFire reference counting.
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction.
If other af::features/af_features references exist, underlying resources may persist until all references are released.

functions.name: af::features::operator=
functions.signature: af::features &af::features::operator=(const af::features &other)
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Assigns this object from another features object, typically updating reference counts to share underlying data.
requirements: Available when AF_API_VERSION >= 38 (per header section).
other must be a valid, initialized af::features object.
Self-assignment is supported by typical implementations but not explicitly documented.

functions.name: af::features::operator=
functions.signature: af::features &af::features::operator=(af::features &&other)
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers ownership of resources from other into this object, releasing any current resources held by this object.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 38 and AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled.
other must be a valid af::features rvalue.
After the move, do not rely on other’s contents; it remains valid but unspecified.

functions.name: af::features::getNumFeatures
functions.signature: size_t af::features::getNumFeatures() const
functions.description: Returns the number of features represented by this object.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.

functions.name: af::features::getX
functions.signature: af::array af::features::getX() const
functions.description: Returns an af::array containing the x-coordinates of all features in this object.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.
Returned array length matches the number of features.

functions.name: af::features::getY
functions.signature: af::array af::features::getY() const
functions.description: Returns an af::array containing the y-coordinates of all features in this object.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.
Returned array length matches the number of features.

functions.name: af::features::getScore
functions.signature: af::array af::features::getScore() const
functions.description: Returns an af::array containing the detection scores of the features.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.
Returned array length matches the number of features.

functions.name: af::features::getOrientation
functions.signature: af::array af::features::getOrientation() const
functions.description: Returns an af::array containing the orientations of the features.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.
Returned array length matches the number of features.

functions.name: af::features::getSize
functions.signature: af::array af::features::getSize() const
functions.description: Returns an af::array containing the sizes (e.g., scale/radius) of the features.
requirements: This must be called on a valid, initialized af::features instance.
Returned array length matches the number of features.

functions.name: af::features::get
functions.signature: af_features af::features::get() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying C API handle (af_features) managed by this object for interoperability with the C API.
requirements: The returned handle remains owned by this af::features object. Do not release it directly with af_release_features while still managed here.
Handle remains valid as long as this af::features (or retained copies) remains alive.

functions.name: af_create_features
functions.signature: af_err af_create_features(af_features *feat, dim_t num)
functions.description: Creates a new af_features object that can hold num features.
requirements: feat must be a non-null pointer to receive the created handle.
num specifies the number of features; must be representable in dim_t. Values are library-defined; negative values (if dim_t is signed) are invalid.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
On failure, *feat is unspecified and must not be used.

functions.name: af_retain_features
functions.signature: af_err af_retain_features(af_features *out, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Increments the reference count of feat and all of its associated arrays, returning a retained handle via out.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the retained handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle obtained from the ArrayFire API and not previously released.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
After success, out references the same underlying object with incremented reference count.

functions.name: af_get_features_num
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_num(dim_t *num, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Retrieves the number of features stored in feat.
requirements: num must be a non-null pointer to receive the count.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_get_features_xpos
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_xpos(af_array *out, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Returns an af_array containing the x positions of the features in feat.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the array handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned af_array per ArrayFire rules.

functions.name: af_get_features_ypos
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_ypos(af_array *out, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Returns an af_array containing the y positions of the features in feat.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the array handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned af_array per ArrayFire rules.

functions.name: af_get_features_score
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_score(af_array *score, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Returns an af_array containing the scores of the features in feat.
requirements: score must be a non-null pointer to receive the array handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned af_array per ArrayFire rules.

functions.name: af_get_features_orientation
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_orientation(af_array *orientation, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Returns an af_array containing feature orientations for feat.
requirements: orientation must be a non-null pointer to receive the array handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned af_array per ArrayFire rules.

functions.name: af_get_features_size
functions.signature: af_err af_get_features_size(af_array *size, const af_features feat)
functions.description: Returns an af_array containing the sizes of the features in feat.
requirements: size must be a non-null pointer to receive the array handle.
feat must be a valid af_features handle.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; callers must check the returned af_err.
The caller is responsible for managing the lifecycle of the returned af_array per ArrayFire rules.

functions.name: af_release_features
functions.signature: af_err af_release_features(af_features feat)
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of feat and releases it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: feat must be a valid af_features handle; passing an invalid or already released handle results in undefined behavior or an error code.

functions.name: af::gforToggle

Intended primarily for internal/macro use; callers should not rely on specific state semantics beyond a boolean toggle behavior.

functions.name: af::gforGet

functions.description: Returns the current internal gfor state flag. Useful for checking whether gfor-mode is active. Primarily intended for internal use alongside the gfor macro.

functions.name: af::gforSet

functions.name: af::batchFunc

Shape compatibility and batching behavior are not specified in this header; callers should ensure lhs and rhs are compatible per ArrayFire’s batching rules.

functions.name: af::Window::Window

functions.name: af::Window::Window

functions.name: af::Window::~Window
functions.signature: af::Window::~Window()
functions.description: Destructor. Destroys/releases the underlying window handle and associated resources.

functions.name: af::Window::get
functions.signature: af_window af::Window::get() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying af_window handle for interop or use with the C API.

functions.name: af::Window::setPos

functions.name: af::loadImage
functions.signature: AFAPI array loadImage(const char* filename, const bool is_color=false);
functions.description: Loads an image from disk into an af::array. If is_color is true, loads a 3-channel image; otherwise loads a single-channel image.
requirements: filename must point to a valid, readable image file path
is_color selects 3-channel (true) or 1-channel (false) output

functions.name: af::saveImage
functions.signature: AFAPI void saveImage(const char* filename, const array& in);
functions.description: Saves the input af::array as an image to disk.
requirements: filename must be a writable path for the chosen image format (deduced by extension)
in must be a valid af::array with an image-compatible type and shape as supported by ArrayFire/FreeImage

functions.name: af::loadImageMem
functions.signature: AFAPI array loadImageMem(const void *ptr);
functions.description: Loads an image from an in-memory FreeImage FIMEMORY stream pointer into an af::array. Pointer can originate from saveImageMem, af_save_image_memory, or FreeImage_OpenMemory.
requirements: ptr must be a valid pointer to a FreeImage FIMEMORY stream
The memory stream must contain a valid encoded image

functions.name: af::saveImageMem
functions.signature: AFAPI void* saveImageMem(const array& in, const imageFormat format = AF_FIF_PNG);
functions.description: Encodes an image from an af::array into a FreeImage memory stream, returning a FIMEMORY* as void*. The caller must release it using deleteImageMem.
requirements: in must be a valid af::array with an image-compatible type/shape
format must be a valid value from imageFormat (compatible with FreeImage)
Caller must later pass the returned pointer to deleteImageMem to avoid leaks

functions.name: af::deleteImageMem
functions.signature: AFAPI void deleteImageMem(void *ptr);
functions.description: Deletes an in-memory image stream created by saveImageMem/af_save_image_memory/FreeImage_OpenMemory.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously obtained from saveImageMem, af_save_image_memory, or FreeImage_OpenMemory

functions.name: af::loadImageNative
functions.signature: AFAPI array loadImageNative(const char* filename);
functions.description: Loads an image from disk preserving its native component bit-depth: u8 for 8-bit, u16 for 16-bit, and f32 for 32-bit images.
requirements: filename must point to a valid, readable image file
Result type depends on file bit-depth as documented

functions.name: af::saveImageNative
functions.signature: AFAPI void saveImageNative(const char* filename, const array& in);
functions.description: Saves an image without modification to values: only u8, u16, or f32 arrays are accepted and written at 8/16/32 bits per component respectively.
requirements: in must be type u8, u16, or f32 only
filename must be a writable path
Not all image formats support 16/32-bit; recommended: PNG/PPM/TIFF for 16-bit, TIFF for 32-bit

functions.name: af::isImageIOAvailable
functions.signature: AFAPI bool isImageIOAvailable();
functions.description: Returns true if ArrayFire was compiled with ImageIO support, false otherwise.

functions.name: af::resize
functions.signature: AFAPI array resize(const array& in, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Resizes an image to explicit output dimensions using the specified interpolation method.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
odim0 and odim1 specify output height and width (first and second dims)
method is an interpolation type; default AF_INTERP_NEAREST

functions.name: af::resize
functions.signature: AFAPI array resize(const float scale0, const float scale1, const array& in, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Resizes an image by independent scale factors along the first and second dimensions using the specified interpolation method.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
scale0 and scale1 are scale factors for dims 0 and 1
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::resize
functions.signature: AFAPI array resize(const float scale, const array& in, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Uniformly scales an image by the same factor in both dimensions using the specified interpolation method.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
scale is a scalar factor applied to dims 0 and 1
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::rotate
functions.signature: AFAPI array rotate(const array& in, const float theta, const bool crop=true, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Rotates an image by theta radians. Optionally crops to original dimensions or expands to fit. Uses the specified interpolation method.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
theta is in radians
crop=true keeps original size; crop=false expands output
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::transform
functions.signature: AFAPI array transform(const array& in, const array& transform, const dim_t odim0 = 0, const dim_t odim1 = 0, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST, const bool inverse=true);
functions.description: Applies a 2D geometric transform to an image using the provided transformation matrix. Optionally specify output dimensions, interpolation, and whether to apply the inverse mapping.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
transform must be a valid transformation matrix array
odim0/odim1 can specify output size; 0 implies inferred default
inverse=true applies inverse transform; false applies forward
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::transformCoordinates
functions.signature: AFAPI array transformCoordinates(const array& tf, const float d0, const float d1);
functions.description: Transforms 2D coordinates (d0,d1) using the given transformation matrix tf and returns transformed coordinates.
requirements: tf must be a valid transformation matrix array
d0 and d1 are input coordinates (floats)

functions.name: af::translate
functions.signature: AFAPI array translate(const array& in, const float trans0, const float trans1, const dim_t odim0 = 0, const dim_t odim1 = 0, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Translates an image by specified offsets along the first and second dimensions. Output size can be specified; interpolation controls resampling.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
trans0 and trans1 are translation amounts
odim0/odim1 optionally specify output size (0 for default)
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::scale
functions.signature: AFAPI array scale(const array& in, const float scale0, const float scale1, const dim_t odim0 = 0, const dim_t odim1 = 0, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Scales an image by independent factors along the first and second dimensions. Output size can be specified; uses given interpolation method.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
scale0 and scale1 are scale factors
odim0/odim1 optionally specify output size (0 for default)
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::skew
functions.signature: AFAPI array skew(const array& in, const float skew0, const float skew1, const dim_t odim0 = 0, const dim_t odim1 = 0, const bool inverse=true, const interpType method=AF_INTERP_NEAREST);
functions.description: Applies a skew (shear) transform to an image. Can apply inverse or forward transform and specify output size and interpolation.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
skew0 and skew1 control shear along first and second dimensions
odim0/odim1 optionally specify output size (0 for default)
inverse selects inverse or forward transform
method is an interpolation type

functions.name: af::bilateral
functions.signature: AFAPI array bilateral(const array &in, const float spatial_sigma, const float chromatic_sigma, const bool is_color=false);
functions.description: Applies bilateral filtering to smooth an image while preserving edges. Supports grayscale and color images.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
spatial_sigma controls spatial kernel/window extent
chromatic_sigma controls range/color similarity
is_color indicates if in is color (true) or grayscale (false)

functions.name: af::histogram
functions.signature: AFAPI array histogram(const array &in, const unsigned nbins, const double minval, const double maxval);
functions.description: Computes a histogram with nbins over the input value range [minval, maxval], returning a u32 histogram array.
requirements: in must be a valid array
nbins is the number of bins
minval is the minimum bin value (accumulates -inf to min)
maxval is the maximum bin value (accumulates max to +inf)

functions.name: af::histogram
functions.signature: AFAPI array histogram(const array &in, const unsigned nbins);
functions.description: Computes a histogram with nbins over the input’s dynamic range, returning a u32 histogram array.
requirements: in must be a valid array
nbins is the number of bins

functions.name: af::meanShift
functions.signature: AFAPI array meanShift(const array& in, const float spatial_sigma, const float chromatic_sigma, const unsigned iter, const bool is_color=false);
functions.description: Performs mean shift filtering for edge-preserving smoothing and mode seeking in joint spatial-chromatic space.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
spatial_sigma controls spatial kernel extent
chromatic_sigma controls range/color similarity
iter is the number of iterations
is_color indicates if in is color (true) or grayscale (false)

functions.name: af::minfilt
functions.signature: AFAPI array minfilt(const array& in, const dim_t wind_length = 3, const dim_t wind_width = 3, const borderType edge_pad = AF_PAD_ZERO);
functions.description: Applies a minimum filter (morphological erosion with all-ones mask) over a window, with specified border handling.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
wind_length and wind_width specify kernel height and width
edge_pad must be AF_PAD_ZERO or AF_PAD_SYM

functions.name: af::maxfilt
functions.signature: AFAPI array maxfilt(const array& in, const dim_t wind_length = 3, const dim_t wind_width = 3, const borderType edge_pad = AF_PAD_ZERO);
functions.description: Applies a maximum filter (morphological dilation with all-ones mask) over a window, with specified border handling.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
wind_length and wind_width specify kernel height and width
edge_pad must be AF_PAD_ZERO or AF_PAD_SYM

functions.name: af::dilate
functions.signature: AFAPI array dilate(const array& in, const array& mask);
functions.description: Performs grayscale image dilation using the provided neighborhood mask. Equivalent to max filter if mask is all ones.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
mask must be a valid neighborhood window array; all-ones mask behaves like max filter

functions.name: af::dilate3
functions.signature: AFAPI array dilate3(const array& in, const array& mask);
functions.description: Performs 3D grayscale dilation on a volume using the provided 3D neighborhood mask.
requirements: in must be a valid 3D volume array
mask must be a valid 3D neighborhood (delta volume) array

functions.name: af::erode
functions.signature: AFAPI array erode(const array& in, const array& mask);
functions.description: Performs grayscale image erosion using the provided neighborhood mask. Can be used as min filter if mask is all ones.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
mask must be a valid neighborhood window array; all-ones mask behaves like min filter

functions.name: af::erode3
functions.signature: AFAPI array erode3(const array& in, const array& mask);
functions.description: Performs 3D grayscale erosion on a volume using the provided 3D neighborhood mask.
requirements: in must be a valid 3D volume array
mask must be a valid 3D neighborhood (delta volume) array

functions.name: af::regions
functions.signature: AFAPI array regions(const array& in, const af::connectivity connectivity=AF_CONNECTIVITY_4, const dtype type=f32);
functions.description: Labels connected regions in a binary image using the specified connectivity, returning an array of labels of the requested dtype.
requirements: in must be a binary image of type b8
connectivity must be AF_CONNECTIVITY_4 or AF_CONNECTIVITY_8
type selects output array dtype

functions.name: af::sobel
functions.signature: AFAPI void sobel(array &dx, array &dy, const array &img, const unsigned ker_size=3);
functions.description: Computes Sobel gradients Gx and Gy for the input image using a kernel of size ker_size. Batched if img is 3D.
requirements: dx and dy are output arrays passed by non-const reference and will be overwritten
img must be a valid image array
ker_size is Sobel kernel size/window size
If img is 3D, operation is batched

functions.name: af::sobel
functions.signature: AFAPI array sobel(const array &img, const unsigned ker_size=3, const bool isFast=false);
functions.description: Applies Sobel filtering and returns gradient magnitude. If isFast=true, uses L1 norm (Gx+Gy); otherwise uses L2 norm sqrt(Gx^2+Gy^2). Batched if img is 3D.
requirements: img must be a valid image array
ker_size is Sobel kernel size/window size
isFast selects L1 (true) vs L2 (false) magnitude

functions.name: af::rgb2gray
functions.signature: AFAPI array rgb2gray(const array& in, const float rPercent=0.2126f, const float gPercent=0.7152f, const float bPercent=0.0722f);
functions.description: Converts an RGB image to grayscale using specified channel weights.
requirements: in must be three dimensional for RGB to Grayscale conversion
rPercent, gPercent, bPercent are weight fractions contributing to intensity

functions.name: af::gray2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI array gray2rgb(const array& in, const float rFactor=1.0, const float gFactor=1.0, const float bFactor=1.0);
functions.description: Converts a grayscale image to RGB by scaling the intensity into R, G, B channels using the provided factors.
requirements: in must be two dimensional for Grayscale to RGB conversion

functions.name: af::histEqual
functions.signature: AFAPI array histEqual(const array& in, const array& hist);
functions.description: Performs histogram equalization to approximate the target histogram on the input data.
requirements: in must be two dimensional
in is non-normalized and assumes values in [0-255]
hist is a target histogram array (bins determine mapping)

functions.name: af::gaussianKernel
functions.signature: AFAPI array gaussianKernel(const int rows, const int cols, const double sig_r = 0, const double sig_c = 0);
functions.description: Generates a 2D Gaussian kernel of given size and standard deviations. If sigmas are 0, they are computed as 0.25*size + 0.75 per dimension.
requirements: rows and cols specify kernel dimensions
sig_r and sig_c are standard deviations; if 0, computed internally as documented

functions.name: af::hsv2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI array hsv2rgb(const array& in);
functions.description: Converts an HSV image to RGB.
requirements: in must be three dimensional

functions.name: af::rgb2hsv
functions.signature: AFAPI array rgb2hsv(const array& in);
functions.description: Converts an RGB image to HSV.
requirements: in must be three dimensional

functions.name: af::colorSpace
functions.signature: AFAPI array colorSpace(const array& image, const CSpace to, const CSpace from);
functions.description: Converts an image between color spaces as specified by from and to.
requirements: image must be 3D for HSV<->RGB and RGB->GRAY conversions; 2D for GRAY->RGB
to and from must be valid CSpace values

functions.name: af::unwrap
functions.signature: AFAPI array unwrap(const array& in, const dim_t wx, const dim_t wy, const dim_t sx, const dim_t sy, const dim_t px=0, const dim_t py=0, const bool is_column = true);
functions.description: Extracts sliding window patches from an image and rearranges them into columns (or rows). Supports batched operation for 3D/4D inputs.
requirements: in can be 2D; batched if 3D/4D
wx and wy must be between [1, input.dims(0/1) + px/py]
sx and sy must be greater than 1
px and py must be between [0, wx(wy) - 1]; padding is applied prior to windowing
is_column selects column (true) or row (false) layout

functions.name: af::wrap
functions.signature: AFAPI array wrap(const array& in, const dim_t ox, const dim_t oy, const dim_t wx, const dim_t wy, const dim_t sx, const dim_t sy, const dim_t px = 0, const dim_t py = 0, const bool is_column = true);
functions.description: Inverse of unwrap: reshapes columns/rows of patches back into an image of size ox x oy. Supports batched operation.
requirements: Use same parameters used for unwrap when recomposing; ox/oy are original image size
wx*wy must equal input.dims(0) if is_column=true (or input.dims(1) if false)
sx and sy must be at least 1
px in [0, wx), py in [0, wy)
Number of patches must be nx*ny where nx=(ox+2px-wx)/sx+1 and ny=(oy+2py-wy)/sy+1
Batched wrap allowed if input is 3D/4D

functions.name: af::sat
functions.signature: AFAPI array sat(const array& in);
functions.description: Computes the summed area table (integral image) of the input array.
requirements: in must be a valid array

functions.name: af::ycbcr2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI array ycbcr2rgb(const array& in, const YCCStd standard=AF_YCC_601);
functions.description: Converts a YCbCr image to RGB using the specified ITU-R BT standard to determine conversion constants.
requirements: in must be three dimensional
Input values should lie in the range [0,1]
standard must be a valid YCCStd

functions.name: af::rgb2ycbcr
functions.signature: AFAPI array rgb2ycbcr(const array& in, const YCCStd standard=AF_YCC_601);
functions.description: Converts an RGB image to YCbCr using the specified ITU-R BT standard.
requirements: in must be three dimensional
Input values should lie in the range [0,1]
standard must be a valid YCCStd

functions.name: af::moments
functions.signature: AFAPI void moments(double* out, const array& in, const momentType moment=AF_MOMENT_FIRST_ORDER);
functions.description: Computes specified image moment(s) of a single image and writes the results to a user-provided buffer.
requirements: out must point to pre-allocated memory sufficient to hold all requested moments
in must be a valid image array
moment selects which moments to compute

functions.name: af::moments
functions.signature: AFAPI array moments(const array& in, const momentType moment=AF_MOMENT_FIRST_ORDER);
functions.description: Computes specified image moment(s) of one or more images, returning the results in an array.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
moment selects which moments to compute

functions.name: af::canny
functions.signature: AFAPI array canny(const array& in, const cannyThreshold thresholdType, const float lowThresholdRatio, const float highThresholdRatio, const unsigned sobelWindow = 3, const bool isFast = false);
functions.description: Runs the Canny edge detector on the input image, returning a binary edge map. Supports user or automatic high threshold selection and Sobel window size and norm choice.
requirements: in must be a valid image array
thresholdType must be a valid af_canny_threshold value; if AF_CANNY_THRESHOLD_AUTO_OTSU, highThresholdRatio is ignored
lowThresholdRatio is the lower ratio of the max or auto-derived high threshold
highThresholdRatio is the higher ratio (ignored for AUTO_OTSU)
sobelWindow is the Sobel kernel size
isFast selects L1 (true) vs L2 (false) gradient magnitude

functions.name: af::anisotropicDiffusion
functions.signature: AFAPI array anisotropicDiffusion(const af::array& in, const float timestep, const float conductance, const unsigned iterations, const fluxFunction fftype=AF_FLUX_EXPONENTIAL, const diffusionEq diffusionKind=AF_DIFFUSION_GRAD);
functions.description: Performs gradient- or curvature-based anisotropic diffusion (nonlinear smoothing) on an image using the specified flux function and diffusion equation.
requirements: in must be a float/double (non-integral) typed af::array
timestep controls the diffusion time step
conductance controls conductance sensitivity
iterations is the number of diffusion steps
fftype selects quadratic or exponential flux
diffusionKind selects the diffusion method (enum diffusionEq)

functions.name: af::iterativeDeconv
functions.signature: AFAPI array iterativeDeconv(const array& in, const array& ker, const unsigned iterations, const float relaxFactor, const iterativeDeconvAlgo algo);
functions.description: Performs iterative deconvolution using the specified algorithm (e.g., Richardson-Lucy, etc.) with a given PSF kernel and iteration count. relaxFactor is ignored for Richardson–Lucy.
requirements: in must be a blurred image array
ker must be the known point spread function (kernel) array
iterations is the number of algorithm iterations
relaxFactor is a relaxation factor; ignored for AF_ITERATIVE_DECONV_RICHARDSONLUCY
algo must be a valid iterativeDeconvAlgo

functions.name: af::inverseDeconv
functions.signature: AFAPI array inverseDeconv(const array& in, const array& psf, const float gamma, const inverseDeconvAlgo algo);
functions.description: Performs inverse deconvolution (e.g., Tikhonov) using the provided PSF. For AF_INVERSE_DECONV_TIKHONOV, gamma is the regularization constant.
requirements: in must be a blurred image array
psf must be the known point spread function array
gamma usage depends on algo; for AF_INVERSE_DECONV_TIKHONOV it is a regularization constant
algo must be a valid inverseDeconvAlgo

functions.name: af::confidenceCC
functions.signature: AFAPI array confidenceCC(const array &in, const array &seeds, const unsigned radius, const unsigned multiplier, const int iter, const double segmentedValue);
functions.description: Segments confidence-connected components starting from seed points provided as (x,y) coordinate columns. Produces an output image with segmented pixels set to segmentedValue.
requirements: in must be a float/double typed image array (non-integral)
seeds must contain x and y coordinates in columns (non-interleaved)
radius specifies neighborhood size considered per seed
multiplier controls threshold range from neighborhood mean/variance
iter is the number of iterations
segmentedValue is the output value for valid pixels

functions.name: af::confidenceCC
functions.signature: AFAPI array confidenceCC(const array &in, const array &seedx, const array &seedy, const unsigned radius, const unsigned multiplier, const int iter, const double segmentedValue);
functions.description: Segments confidence-connected components using separate arrays of x and y seed coordinates.
requirements: in must be a float/double typed image array (non-integral)
seedx contains x coordinates; seedy contains y coordinates
radius specifies neighborhood size
multiplier controls threshold range
iter is the number of iterations
segmentedValue is the output value for valid pixels

functions.name: af::confidenceCC
functions.signature: AFAPI array confidenceCC(const array &in, const size_t num_seeds, const unsigned *seedx, const unsigned *seedy, const unsigned radius, const unsigned multiplier, const int iter, const double segmentedValue);
functions.description: Segments confidence-connected components using raw arrays of seed coordinates of length num_seeds.
requirements: in must be a float/double typed image array (non-integral)
seedx and seedy must each point to arrays of length num_seeds
radius specifies neighborhood size
multiplier controls threshold range
iter is the number of iterations
segmentedValue is the output value for valid pixels

functions.name: af_gradient
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_gradient(af_array *dx, af_array *dy, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Computes gradients of input along first and second dimensions and returns them via dx and dy.
requirements: dx and dy must be valid, non-null pointers to receive af_array handles
in must be a valid af_array

functions.name: af_load_image
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_load_image(af_array *out, const char* filename, const bool isColor);
functions.description: C API: Loads an image from disk; outputs a 1-channel or 3-channel array based on isColor.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
filename must point to a readable image path
isColor selects 3-channel (true) or 1-channel (false) output

functions.name: af_save_image
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_save_image(const char* filename, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Saves an af_array as an image file.
requirements: filename must be a writable path
in must be a valid af_array with supported shape/type for image saving

functions.name: af_load_image_memory
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_load_image_memory(af_array *out, const void* ptr);
functions.description: C API: Loads an image from a FreeImage FIMEMORY pointer into an af_array.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
ptr must point to a valid FIMEMORY containing an encoded image

functions.name: af_save_image_memory
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_save_image_memory(void** ptr, const af_array in, const af_image_format format);
functions.description: C API: Saves an af_array as an encoded image into a FreeImage memory stream, returning a FIMEMORY* via ptr.
requirements: ptr must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the FIMEMORY*
in must be a valid image-compatible af_array
format must be a valid af_image_format/FreeImage format value
Caller is responsible for later freeing the memory using af_delete_image_memory or equivalent

functions.name: af_delete_image_memory
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_delete_image_memory(void* ptr);
functions.description: C API: Deletes a FreeImage FIMEMORY stream previously created by save-to-memory APIs.
requirements: ptr must be a valid FIMEMORY pointer previously returned by af_save_image_memory/saveImageMem/FreeImage_OpenMemory

functions.name: af_load_image_native
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_load_image_native(af_array *out, const char* filename);
functions.description: C API: Loads an image preserving native bit depth (u8/u16/f32).
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
filename must be a valid readable file path

functions.name: af_save_image_native
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_save_image_native(const char* filename, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Saves an image without modifying values; accepts u8, u16, or f32 arrays and writes 8/16/32 bpc respectively.
requirements: filename must be a writable path
in must be type u8, u16, or f32

functions.name: af_is_image_io_available
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_is_image_io_available(bool *out);
functions.description: C API: Reports if ArrayFire is compiled with ImageIO support.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to a bool

functions.name: af_resize
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_resize(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method);
functions.description: C API: Resizes an image to explicit output dimensions using the specified interpolation method.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
odim0 and odim1 are output sizes
method must be a valid af_interp_type

functions.name: af_transform
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_transform(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array transform, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method, const bool inverse);
