functions.description: C API: Applies a geometric transform to an image using a transformation matrix, optional output size, interpolation, and inverse flag.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
transform must be a valid transformation matrix af_array
odim0/odim1 specify output size
method must be a valid af_interp_type
inverse selects inverse or forward mapping

functions.name: af_transform_v2
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_transform_v2(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array transform, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method, const bool inverse);
functions.description: C API: Variant of af_transform that accepts a preallocated output array; may overwrite only the relevant sub-array region.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to an existing or null af_array; passing an uninitialized af_array causes undefined behavior
If out refers to a sub-array, only that region is overwritten
in and transform must be valid af_array objects
odim0/odim1 specify output size
method must be a valid af_interp_type
inverse selects inverse or forward mapping

functions.name: af_transform_coordinates
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_transform_coordinates(af_array *out, const af_array tf, const float d0, const float d1);
functions.description: C API: Transforms coordinates (d0,d1) by the transformation matrix tf and returns transformed coordinates.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
tf must be a valid transformation matrix af_array
d0 and d1 are input coordinates

functions.name: af_rotate
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_rotate(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float theta, const bool crop, const af_interp_type method);
functions.description: C API: Rotates an image by theta radians, optionally cropping to original size, using the specified interpolation method.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
theta is in radians
crop controls output size behavior
method must be a valid af_interp_type

functions.name: af_translate
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_translate(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float trans0, const float trans1, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method);
functions.description: C API: Translates an image by specified offsets; output size and interpolation can be specified.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
trans0 and trans1 are translation amounts
odim0 and odim1 specify output size
method must be a valid af_interp_type

functions.name: af_scale
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_scale(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float scale0, const float scale1, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method);
functions.description: C API: Scales an image by independent factors along the first and second dimensions with specified output size and interpolation.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
scale0 and scale1 are scaling factors
odim0 and odim1 specify output size
method must be a valid af_interp_type

functions.name: af_skew
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_skew(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float skew0, const float skew1, const dim_t odim0, const dim_t odim1, const af_interp_type method, const bool inverse);
functions.description: C API: Applies a skew (shear) transform with optional inverse mapping, output size, and interpolation.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
skew0 and skew1 are shear amounts
odim0 and odim1 specify output size
method must be a valid af_interp_type
inverse selects inverse or forward mapping

functions.name: af_histogram
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_histogram(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned nbins, const double minval, const double maxval);
functions.description: C API: Computes a histogram with nbins between minval and maxval; returns u32 histogram array.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid af_array
nbins is number of bins
minval and maxval define histogram range with underflow/overflow accumulation as documented

functions.name: af_dilate
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_dilate(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array mask);
functions.description: C API: Performs grayscale dilation using the provided mask.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the af_array
in must be a valid image af_array
mask must be a valid neighborhood window af_array

functions.name: af_dilate3
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_dilate3(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array mask);
functions.description: C API: Performs 3D grayscale dilation on a volume using the provided 3D mask.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid 3D af_array
mask must be a valid 3D neighborhood af_array

functions.name: af_erode
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_erode(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array mask);
functions.description: C API: Performs grayscale erosion using the provided mask.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid image af_array
mask must be a valid neighborhood window af_array

functions.name: af_erode3
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_erode3(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array mask);
functions.description: C API: Performs 3D grayscale erosion on a volume using the provided 3D mask.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid 3D af_array
mask must be a valid 3D neighborhood af_array

functions.name: af_bilateral
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_bilateral(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float spatial_sigma, const float chromatic_sigma, const bool isColor);
functions.description: C API: Applies bilateral filtering to an image.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
spatial_sigma and chromatic_sigma must be provided
isColor indicates color vs grayscale input

functions.name: af_mean_shift
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_mean_shift(af_array *out, const af_array in, const float spatial_sigma, const float chromatic_sigma, const unsigned iter, const bool is_color);
functions.description: C API: Applies mean shift filtering for edge-preserving smoothing.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
spatial_sigma and chromatic_sigma must be provided
iter is the iteration count
is_color indicates color vs grayscale

functions.name: af_minfilt
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_minfilt(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t wind_length, const dim_t wind_width, const af_border_type edge_pad);
functions.description: C API: Applies a minimum filter with specified window and border handling.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
wind_length and wind_width specify kernel size
edge_pad must be AF_PAD_ZERO or AF_PAD_SYM

functions.name: af_maxfilt
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_maxfilt(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t wind_length, const dim_t wind_width, const af_border_type edge_pad);
functions.description: C API: Applies a maximum filter with specified window and border handling.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
wind_length and wind_width specify kernel size
edge_pad must be AF_PAD_ZERO or AF_PAD_SYM

functions.name: af_regions
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_regions(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_connectivity connectivity, const af_dtype ty);
functions.description: C API: Labels connected regions in a binary image using the specified connectivity and returns labels with the requested dtype.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a binary image of type b8
connectivity must be AF_CONNECTIVITY_4 or AF_CONNECTIVITY_8
ty selects output dtype

functions.name: af_sobel_operator
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_sobel_operator(af_array *dx, af_array *dy, const af_array img, const unsigned ker_size);
functions.description: C API: Computes Sobel derivatives along horizontal and vertical directions.
requirements: dx and dy must be valid, non-null pointers to receive outputs
img must be a valid af_array
ker_size is Sobel kernel/window size
If img is 3D, operation is batched

functions.name: af_rgb2gray
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_rgb2gray(af_array* out, const af_array in, const float rPercent, const float gPercent, const float bPercent);
functions.description: C API: Converts RGB image to grayscale using provided channel percentages.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 3D RGB af_array
rPercent, gPercent, bPercent specify weights

functions.name: af_gray2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_gray2rgb(af_array* out, const af_array in, const float rFactor, const float gFactor, const float bFactor);
functions.description: C API: Converts grayscale image to RGB by scaling intensity into R, G, B channels using provided factors.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 2D grayscale af_array

functions.name: af_hist_equal
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_hist_equal(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array hist);
functions.description: C API: Performs histogram equalization on a 2D input to approximate a target histogram.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 2D af_array with values assumed in [0-255]
hist is the target histogram array

functions.name: af_gaussian_kernel
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_gaussian_kernel(af_array *out, const int rows, const int cols, const double sigma_r, const double sigma_c);
functions.description: C API: Generates a 2D Gaussian kernel with specified size and sigmas. If a sigma is 0, it will be computed internally as 0.25*size + 0.75.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
rows and cols specify kernel size
sigma_r and sigma_c can be zero to trigger internal computation

functions.name: af_hsv2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_hsv2rgb(af_array* out, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Converts an HSV image to RGB.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 3D HSV af_array

functions.name: af_rgb2hsv
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_rgb2hsv(af_array* out, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Converts an RGB image to HSV.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 3D RGB af_array

functions.name: af_color_space
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_color_space(af_array *out, const af_array image, const af_cspace_t to, const af_cspace_t from);
functions.description: C API: Converts an image between color spaces specified by from and to.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
image must be 3D for HSV<->RGB and RGB->GRAY; 2D for GRAY->RGB
to and from must be valid af_cspace_t values

functions.name: af_unwrap
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_unwrap(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t wx, const dim_t wy, const dim_t sx, const dim_t sy, const dim_t px, const dim_t py, const bool is_column);
functions.description: C API: Rearranges sliding window patches from an input into columns (or rows).
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array; can be 3D/4D for batched processing
wx and wy in [1, input.dims(0/1) + px/py]
sx and sy must be greater than 1
px in [0, wx-1], py in [0, wy-1]
is_column selects columns (true) or rows (false)

functions.name: af_wrap
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_wrap(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t ox, const dim_t oy, const dim_t wx, const dim_t wy, const dim_t sx, const dim_t sy, const dim_t px, const dim_t py, const bool is_column);
functions.description: C API: Inverse of af_unwrap. Reshapes columns/rows of patches back to an image of size ox x oy.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
Use the same parameters used for af_unwrap for recomposition; ox/oy are the original image size
wx*wy must equal input.dims(0) if is_column=true (or input.dims(1) if false)
sx and sy >= 1
px in [0, wx), py in [0, wy)
Number of patches must equal nx*ny with nx=(ox+2px-wx)/sx+1 and ny=(oy+2py-wy)/sy+1
Batched recomposition allowed if in is 3D/4D

functions.name: af_wrap_v2
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_wrap_v2(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t ox, const dim_t oy, const dim_t wx, const dim_t wy, const dim_t sx, const dim_t sy, const dim_t px, const dim_t py, const bool is_column);
functions.description: C API: Variant of af_wrap that accepts a preallocated output array.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to an existing or null af_array
All af_wrap constraints apply for in, ox/oy, wx/wy, sx/sy, px/py, and is_column

functions.name: af_sat
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_sat(af_array *out, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API: Computes the summed area table (integral image) of the input.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array

functions.name: af_ycbcr2rgb
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_ycbcr2rgb(af_array* out, const af_array in, const af_ycc_std standard);
functions.description: C API: Converts YCbCr image to RGB using the specified ITU standard.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 3D af_array with values in [0,1]
standard must be a valid af_ycc_std

functions.name: af_rgb2ycbcr
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_rgb2ycbcr(af_array* out, const af_array in, const af_ycc_std standard);
functions.description: C API: Converts RGB image to YCbCr using the specified ITU standard.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a 3D af_array with values in [0,1]
standard must be a valid af_ycc_std

functions.name: af_moments
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_moments(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_moment_type moment);
functions.description: C API: Computes requested image moments of image(s) and returns them in an array.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
moment selects which moments to compute

functions.name: af_moments_all
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_moments_all(double* out, const af_array in, const af_moment_type moment);
functions.description: C API: Computes requested moment(s) of a single image and writes them into the user-provided buffer.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to pre-allocated memory sufficient for requested moments
in must be a valid af_array
moment selects which moments to compute

functions.name: af_canny
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_canny(af_array* out, const af_array in, const af_canny_threshold threshold_type, const float low_threshold_ratio, const float high_threshold_ratio, const unsigned sobel_window, const bool is_fast);
functions.description: C API: Runs the Canny edge detector and returns a binary edge map.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array
threshold_type must be a valid af_canny_threshold; if AF_CANNY_THRESHOLD_AUTO_OTSU, high_threshold_ratio is ignored
low_threshold_ratio and high_threshold_ratio specify threshold ratios
sobel_window is the Sobel kernel size
is_fast selects L1 vs L2 norm

functions.name: af_anisotropic_diffusion
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_anisotropic_diffusion(af_array* out, const af_array in, const float timestep, const float conductance, const unsigned iterations, const af_flux_function fftype, const af_diffusion_eq diffusion_kind);
functions.description: C API: Performs anisotropic diffusion (gradient or curvature based) on an image using specified parameters.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a float/double typed af_array (non-integral)
timestep, conductance, and iterations must be provided
fftype selects quadratic or exponential flux
diffusion_kind selects diffusion equation

functions.name: af_iterative_deconv
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_iterative_deconv(af_array* out, const af_array in, const af_array ker, const unsigned iterations, const float relax_factor, const af_iterative_deconv_algo algo);
functions.description: C API: Performs iterative deconvolution given a blurred image and PSF. relax_factor is ignored for Richardson–Lucy.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array (blurred image)
ker must be a valid PSF af_array
iterations is the iteration count
relax_factor is used unless algo is AF_ITERATIVE_DECONV_RICHARDSONLUCY
algo must be a valid af_iterative_deconv_algo

functions.name: af_inverse_deconv
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_inverse_deconv(af_array* out, const af_array in, const af_array psf, const float gamma, const af_inverse_deconv_algo algo);
functions.description: C API: Performs inverse deconvolution, including Tikhonov; gamma’s meaning depends on the chosen algorithm (regularization constant for Tikhonov).
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a valid af_array (blurred image)
psf must be a valid PSF af_array
gamma must be provided; for AF_INVERSE_DECONV_TIKHONOV it is the regularization constant
algo must be a valid af_inverse_deconv_algo

functions.name: af_confidence_cc
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_confidence_cc(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array seedx, const af_array seedy, const unsigned radius, const unsigned multiplier, const int iter, const double segmented_value);
functions.description: C API: Performs confidence connected components segmentation using separate seed x and y coordinate arrays.
requirements: out must be a valid, non-null pointer
in must be a float/double typed af_array (non-integral)
seedx and seedy must be valid af_arrays containing seed coordinates
radius, multiplier, iter, and segmented_value must be provided

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index()
functions.description: Default constructor for an index object. Equivalent to af::span (selects entire dimension). Used to build indexers for array slicing.
requirements: No arguments required.
Behavior equivalent to af::span; exact semantics of span are defined by ArrayFire and not elaborated here.

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index(const int idx)
functions.description: Constructs an index representing a single element position using an integer index.
requirements: idx is interpreted as a position along a dimension; valid range is library-defined and not specified in this header (unknown).
Caller must ensure idx refers to a valid location for the target array when used.

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index(const af::seq &s0)
functions.description: Constructs an index from an af::seq object to select a range with begin/end/step.
requirements: s0 must describe a valid sequence for the target array when used (bounds and step semantics are library-defined; exact valid ranges unknown).

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index(const af_seq &s0)
functions.description: Constructs an index from a C-API af_seq object to select a range with begin/end/step.
requirements: s0 must describe a valid sequence for the target array when used (bounds and step semantics are library-defined; exact valid ranges unknown).

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index(const af::array &idx0)
functions.description: Constructs an index from an af::array of indices, enabling gather-style indexing.
requirements: idx0 must be an index array appropriate for the target dimension when used; element type and value constraints are library-defined and not specified here (unknown).
When used, values in idx0 must be within valid index ranges of the source array.

functions.name: af::index::index
functions.signature: af::index::index(const af::index &idx0)
functions.description: Copy constructor for af::index. Creates a new index with the same underlying representation as idx0.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
idx0 must be a valid af::index.

functions.name: af::index::~index
functions.signature: af::index::~index()
functions.description: Destructor for af::index. Releases any internal resources tied to the underlying af_index_t representation.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
No explicit cleanup required by callers; handled by the destructor.

functions.name: af::index::isspan
functions.signature: bool af::index::isspan() const
functions.description: Returns true if this index represents af::span (i.e., selects the full extent of a dimension).
requirements: None.

functions.name: af::index::get
functions.signature: const af_index_t &af::index::get() const
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the underlying C-API af_index_t structure represented by this af::index.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid as long as the af::index object is alive.
Do not modify through this reference (const).

functions.name: af::index::operator=
functions.signature: af::index &af::index::operator=(const af::index &idx0)
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this index with idx0’s representation.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
idx0 must be a valid af::index.

functions.name: af::index::operator=
functions.signature: af::index &af::index::operator=(af::index &&idx0)
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Transfers resources from idx0 to this object, leaving idx0 in a valid but unspecified state.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31 and AF_COMPILER_CXX_RVALUE_REFERENCES is enabled.
idx0 is an rvalue (about to be discarded). Do not rely on idx0’s state after the move.

functions.name: af::lookup
functions.signature: af::array af::lookup(const af::array &in, const af::array &idx, const int dim = -1)
functions.description: Returns elements from in at positions specified by idx along dimension dim (gather operation).
requirements: in must be a valid af::array.
idx must be a valid af::array of indices; required dtype and shape conventions are not specified here (unknown).
dim specifies the dimension for indexing; exact valid range and semantics of default -1 are not specified here (unknown).
Index values in idx must be within bounds of in along dim.

functions.name: af::copy
functions.signature: void af::copy(af::array &dst, const af::array &src, const af::index &idx0, const af::index &idx1 = af::span, const af::index &idx2 = af::span, const af::index &idx3 = af::span)
functions.description: Copies values from src into dst at positions specified by the provided indices (scatter/assignment via indexing). Unspecified positions in dst remain unchanged.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
dst must be a valid, preallocated af::array that can accommodate the assignment defined by indices.
src must be a valid af::array whose shape is compatible with the indexed region of dst (exact broadcasting or shape rules are not specified here; unknown).
idx0 is required; idx1–idx3 default to af::span if not provided.

functions.name: af_index
functions.signature: af_err af_index(af_array *out, const af_array in, const unsigned ndims, const af_seq *const index)
functions.description: Indexes the input array in using a list of sequences and returns the selected values in out.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the result af_array.
in must be a valid af_array.
index must point to an array of length ndims containing valid af_seq values.
ndims is the number of sequences provided; exact allowable range is not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_lookup
functions.signature: af_err af_lookup(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_array indices, const unsigned dim)
functions.description: Indexes input array in using indices along the specified dimension dim, writing the result to out (gather).
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the result af_array.
in and indices must be valid af_array handles.
indices must contain valid index values within the bounds of in along dim; required dtype/shape are not specified here (unknown).
dim specifies the dimension for indexing; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_assign_seq
functions.signature: af_err af_assign_seq(af_array *out, const af_array lhs, const unsigned ndims, const af_seq *const indices, const af_array rhs)
functions.description: Assigns values from rhs into a copy of lhs at positions specified by a list of sequence indices, returning the result in out. Values not covered by indices come from lhs.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the result af_array.
lhs and rhs must be valid af_array handles.
indices must point to an array of length ndims with valid af_seq entries.
ndims is the number of sequences provided; exact allowable range is not specified here (unknown).
Shapes of rhs and the indexed region must be compatible; exact rules are not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_index_gen
functions.signature: af_err af_index_gen(af_array *out, const af_array in, const dim_t ndims, const af_index_t *indices)
functions.description: Generalized indexing using a list of af_index_t objects (each can be an af_seq or af_array). Selects elements from in and writes to out.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the result af_array.
in must be a valid af_array.
indices must point to an array of length ndims with valid af_index_t entries.
ndims is the number of indexers provided; exact allowable range is not specified here (unknown).
Each af_index_t must be properly initialized with either seq or arr and the isSeq/isBatch flags as appropriate.
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_assign_gen
functions.signature: af_err af_assign_gen(af_array *out, const af_array lhs, const dim_t ndims, const af_index_t *indices, const af_array rhs)
functions.description: Generalized assignment using a list of af_index_t objects (each can be an af_seq or af_array). Copies values from rhs into a copy of lhs at the indexed positions, returning the result in out.
requirements: out must be a non-null pointer to receive the result af_array.
lhs and rhs must be valid af_array handles.
indices must point to an array of length ndims with valid af_index_t entries.
ndims is the number of indexers provided; exact allowable range is not specified here (unknown).
Shapes of rhs and the indexed region of lhs must be compatible; exact rules are not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_create_indexers
functions.signature: af_err af_create_indexers(af_index_t **indexers)
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a quadruple of af_index_t objects for later configuration with per-dimension indexers.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
indexers must be a non-null pointer to receive the allocated array of four af_index_t items.
Caller is responsible for releasing the allocated indexers via af_release_indexers.
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_set_array_indexer
functions.signature: af_err af_set_array_indexer(af_index_t *indexer, const af_array idx, const dim_t dim)
functions.description: Sets the indexer for a given dimension dim to use an af_array of indices.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
indexer must point to the previously created quadruple af_index_t array (from af_create_indexers).
idx must be a valid af_array containing indices; required dtype/shape are not specified here (unknown).
dim is the dimension to be indexed; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_set_seq_indexer
functions.signature: af_err af_set_seq_indexer(af_index_t *indexer, const af_seq *idx, const dim_t dim, const bool is_batch)
functions.description: Sets the indexer for a given dimension dim to use an af_seq range. Supports marking the sequence as a batch parameter.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
indexer must point to the previously created quadruple af_index_t array (from af_create_indexers).
idx must be a non-null pointer to a valid af_seq.
dim is the dimension to be indexed; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
is_batch indicates batched indexing; meaning is library-defined and not elaborated here.
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_set_seq_param_indexer
functions.signature: af_err af_set_seq_param_indexer(af_index_t *indexer, const double begin, const double end, const double step, const dim_t dim, const bool is_batch)
functions.description: Sets the indexer for a given dimension dim using begin/end/step parameters to construct an af_seq internally. Supports batched indexing.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
indexer must point to the previously created quadruple af_index_t array (from af_create_indexers).
begin, end, and step define the sequence; valid ranges and step constraints are library-defined and not specified here (unknown).
dim is the dimension to be indexed; valid range is not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af_release_indexers
functions.signature: af_err af_release_indexers(af_index_t *indexers)
functions.description: Releases the memory resources used by the quadruple af_index_t array created by af_create_indexers.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
indexers must be a pointer previously returned by af_create_indexers.
Do not use indexers after releasing.
Caller must check the returned af_err for success or failure.

functions.name: af::createStridedArray
functions.signature: af::array createStridedArray(const void *data, const dim_t offset, const af::dim4 dims, const af::dim4 strides, const af::dtype ty, const af::source location);
functions.description: Creates an af::array that views raw memory with a specified element offset, dimensions, and element-wise strides. If location is afHost, the data is copied into device memory; otherwise the pointer is treated as already resident on the target backend. Typical usage is to wrap or subview externally managed memory or to construct a non-contiguous view.
requirements: data must point to a buffer compatible with ty and to host or device memory matching location (inferred).
offset is specified in number of elements from data (explicit).
dims defines the region-of-interest shape in elements (explicit).
strides specifies the element-to-element distance along each dimension in elements (explicit).
dims and strides must describe a valid, in-bounds region relative to data and offset; the caller must ensure no out-of-bounds accesses (inferred).
If location is afHost, data must be readable for at least the ROI footprint to permit copying (inferred).

functions.name: af::getStrides
functions.signature: af::dim4 getStrides(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Returns the element-wise distance (strides) between consecutive elements of the input array along each dimension.
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized af::array (inferred).

functions.name: af::getOffset
functions.signature: dim_t getOffset(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Returns the offset, in elements, from the beginning of the underlying raw data pointer to the first element of the array view.
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized af::array (inferred).

functions.name: af::getRawPtr
functions.signature: void *getRawPtr(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer location to the array’s underlying storage. This pointer may be shared by multiple arrays; use with caution.
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized af::array (inferred).
Returned pointer may be shared with other arrays; avoid assuming unique ownership (explicit note).

functions.name: af::isLinear
functions.signature: bool isLinear(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Returns true if all elements of the array are contiguous in memory (i.e., have linear layout).
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized af::array (inferred).

functions.name: af::isOwner
functions.signature: bool isOwner(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Returns true if the array owns its underlying raw pointer; false for subarrays or views of another allocation.
requirements: in must be a valid, initialized af::array (inferred).

functions.name: af_create_strided_array
functions.signature: af_err af_create_strided_array(af_array *arr, const void *data, const dim_t offset, const unsigned ndims, const dim_t *const dims, const dim_t *const strides, const af_dtype ty, const af_source location);
functions.description: Creates an af_array with a specified element offset, dimensions, and element-wise strides from a raw data pointer. If location is afHost, the data is copied; otherwise the pointer is treated as residing on the device/backend.
requirements: arr must be a non-null output pointer to receive the created array (inferred).
data must point to host or device memory matching location and be compatible with ty (inferred).
offset is in number of elements from data (explicit).
ndims specifies the number of dimensions (explicit).
dims must point to an array of at least ndims elements specifying extents in elements (explicit/inferred).
strides must point to an array of at least ndims elements specifying element-wise strides (explicit/inferred).
dims/strides/offset must describe a valid region relative to data; caller must ensure no out-of-bounds access (inferred).
If location is afHost, data must be readable for the ROI footprint to enable copying (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value for success/failure (inferred from C API conventions).

functions.name: af_get_strides
functions.signature: af_err af_get_strides(dim_t *s0, dim_t *s1, dim_t *s2, dim_t *s3, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Retrieves the element-wise distance (stride) between consecutive elements along each of the four dimensions of arr.
requirements: s0, s1, s2, and s3 must be non-null pointers to receive stride values (explicit by out-params, inferred).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af_get_offset
functions.signature: af_err af_get_offset(dim_t *offset, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Retrieves the offset, in elements, from the start of the underlying data pointer to the first element of arr.
requirements: offset must be a non-null pointer to receive the result (explicit by out-param, inferred).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af_get_raw_ptr
functions.signature: af_err af_get_raw_ptr(void **ptr, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Returns the raw pointer location underlying arr via ptr. The pointer may be shared by multiple arrays; use with caution.
requirements: ptr must be a non-null pointer-to-pointer to receive the raw pointer (explicit by out-param, inferred).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Returned pointer may be shared; do not assume unique ownership (explicit note).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af_is_linear
functions.signature: af_err af_is_linear(bool *result, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Determines whether arr is contiguous (linear) in memory and writes the boolean result.
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to receive the boolean (explicit by out-param, inferred).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af_is_owner
functions.signature: af_err af_is_owner(bool *result, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Determines whether arr owns its underlying raw pointer (true) or is a subarray/view (false).
requirements: result must be a non-null pointer to receive the boolean (explicit by out-param, inferred).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af_get_allocated_bytes
functions.signature: af_err af_get_allocated_bytes(size_t *bytes, const af_array arr);
functions.description: Retrieves the size in bytes of the physically allocated buffer backing arr. If arr is an indexed/sub array, returns the size of the parent/owner allocation.
requirements: bytes must be a non-null pointer to receive the size (explicit).
arr must be a valid af_array (inferred).
Function returns af_err; caller must check the return value (inferred).

functions.name: af::svd
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::svd(af::array &u, af::array &s, af::array &vt, const af::array &in);
functions.description: Computes the singular value decomposition of input matrix `in`, producing U, the vector of singular values in `s` (as a diagonal), and V^H in `vt`. Intended for general SVD use.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array representing a matrix.
Outputs `u`, `s`, and `vt` must be lvalues that can be written into by the function.
No explicit size or type restrictions are documented beyond being valid ArrayFire arrays.

functions.name: af::svdInPlace
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::svdInPlace(af::array &u, af::array &s, af::array &vt, af::array &in);
functions.description: Performs in-place singular value decomposition, minimizing memory use by reusing storage from `in`. After the call, `in` contains unspecified/random data.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array with dim0 >= dim1 (number of rows >= number of columns).
`in` is modified and will contain random/undefined data after the operation; do not use it afterwards except as documented.
Outputs `u`, `s`, and `vt` must be valid arrays to receive results.

functions.name: af::lu
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::lu(af::array &out, af::array &pivot, const af::array &in, const bool is_lapack_piv=true);
functions.description: Computes LU decomposition in a packed format from `in`. Returns the packed LU matrix in `out` and the permutation indices in `pivot`. The pivot format can be made LAPACK-compliant via `is_lapack_piv`.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`out` and `pivot` must be writable arrays.
`is_lapack_piv` controls whether the pivot is returned in LAPACK-compliant format.

functions.name: af::lu
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::lu(af::array &lower, af::array &upper, af::array &pivot, const af::array &in);
functions.description: Computes LU decomposition from `in` and returns L (unit or lower triangular) in `lower`, U (upper triangular) in `upper`, and permutation indices in `pivot`.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`lower`, `upper`, and `pivot` must be writable arrays.

functions.name: af::luInPlace
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::luInPlace(af::array &pivot, af::array &in, const bool is_lapack_piv=true);
functions.description: Performs in-place LU decomposition. On exit, `in` contains the packed LU factors and `pivot` contains permutation indices. Pivot format can be LAPACK-compliant.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array and will be overwritten with a packed LU decomposition.
`pivot` must be a writable array to receive permutation indices.
`is_lapack_piv` controls output pivot format.

functions.name: af::qr
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::qr(af::array &out, af::array &tau, const af::array &in);
functions.description: Computes QR decomposition in packed format for `in`. Returns packed QR data in `out` and additional info in `tau` for later unpacking/operations.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`out` and `tau` must be writable arrays.

functions.name: af::qr
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::qr(af::array &q, af::array &r, af::array &tau, const af::array &in);
functions.description: Computes QR decomposition of `in`. Returns orthogonal matrix `q`, upper triangular matrix `r`, and auxiliary vector `tau` useful for least-squares solutions.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`q`, `r`, and `tau` must be writable arrays.

functions.name: af::qrInPlace
functions.signature: AFAPI void af::qrInPlace(af::array &tau, af::array &in);
functions.description: Performs in-place QR decomposition. On exit, `in` holds a packed QR representation; `tau` stores additional data needed to unpack or solve systems.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix) and will be overwritten with packed QR data.
`tau` must be a writable array.

functions.name: af::cholesky
functions.signature: AFAPI int af::cholesky(af::array &out, const af::array &in, const bool is_upper = true);
functions.description: Computes the Cholesky factorization of a positive-definite matrix `in`. Writes the triangular factor to `out` (upper if `is_upper` is true, otherwise lower). Returns 0 on success; otherwise returns the rank at which the decomposition fails.
requirements: `in` must be a positive-definite matrix (2D array).
`out` must be a writable array to receive the triangular factor.
`is_upper` selects whether `out` is upper or lower triangular.
Caller should check the integer return value: 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure rank.

functions.name: af::choleskyInPlace
functions.signature: AFAPI int af::choleskyInPlace(af::array &in, const bool is_upper = true);
functions.description: In-place Cholesky factorization of a positive-definite matrix. Overwrites `in` with its triangular Cholesky factor (upper if `is_upper` is true, else lower). Returns 0 on success; otherwise returns the rank at which factorization fails.
requirements: `in` must be a positive-definite matrix (2D array).
`in` is overwritten with the triangular factor.
`is_upper` selects whether the result is upper or lower triangular.
Caller should check the integer return value for success (0) or failure rank.

functions.name: af::solve
functions.signature: AFAPI af::array af::solve(const af::array &a, const af::array &b, const af::matProp options = AF_MAT_NONE);
functions.description: Solves a linear system A x = B for x. `options` describes properties of `a` (e.g., triangular). Returns the solution array x.
requirements: `a` and `b` must be compatible in dimensions for solving A x = B.
`options` must be one of AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_LOWER, or AF_MAT_UPPER as documented.
Caller must handle any errors via exceptions or status in the environment (not detailed here).

functions.name: af::solveLU
functions.signature: AFAPI af::array af::solveLU(const af::array &a, const af::array &piv, const af::array &b, const af::matProp options = AF_MAT_NONE);
functions.description: Solves a linear system using a precomputed packed LU decomposition `a` with pivot indices `piv`. Returns the solution x to A x = B.
requirements: `a` must be a packed LU decomposition of the coefficient matrix.
`piv` must be the pivot array from the LU decomposition corresponding to `a`.
`b` must be dimensionally compatible with the system.
`options` currently must be AF_MAT_NONE.

functions.name: af::inverse
functions.signature: AFAPI af::array af::inverse(const af::array &in, const af::matProp options = AF_MAT_NONE);
functions.description: Computes the inverse of matrix `in`. The `options` parameter determines properties of `in` (currently must be AF_MAT_NONE). Returns the inverse matrix.
requirements: `in` must be a square, invertible matrix (implied by operation; not explicitly stated).
`options` currently must be AF_MAT_NONE.

functions.name: af::pinverse
functions.signature: AFAPI af::array af::pinverse(const af::array &in, const double tol=1E-6, const af::matProp options = AF_MAT_NONE);
functions.description: Computes the Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse of `in` using an SVD-based method. `tol` influences the threshold used for singular values in the pseudo-inverse.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`tol` defines the lower threshold for singular values; it is passed to the internal threshold calculation relative to `in`.
`options` must be AF_MAT_NONE.

functions.name: af::rank
functions.signature: AFAPI unsigned af::rank(const af::array &in, const double tol=1E-5);
functions.description: Computes the numerical rank of matrix `in` using tolerance `tol`. Returns the rank as an unsigned integer.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
`tol` is a non-negative tolerance used to determine rank (non-negativity inferred; exact constraints not explicitly stated).

functions.name: af::det
functions.signature: template <typename T> T af::det(const af::array &in);
functions.description: Computes the determinant of matrix `in`. Returns the determinant as type T.
requirements: `in` must be a 2D array (matrix).
Template type `T` should match the desired return type of the determinant; exact supported types are not specified in this header.
Behavior for complex inputs and type requirements are not explicitly documented.

functions.name: af::norm
functions.signature: AFAPI double af::norm(const af::array &in, const af::normType type=AF_NORM_EUCLID, const double p=1, const double q=1);
functions.description: Computes a matrix/vector norm of `in`. `type` selects the norm (see af::normType). `p` and `q` are used when type is a P-norm or L_pq matrix norm; otherwise they are ignored.
requirements: `in` must be a valid ArrayFire array (matrix or vector as applicable).
`type` must be a valid af::normType value.
`p` is used only when type is AF_NORM_VECTOR_P or AF_NORM_MATRIX_L_PQ; otherwise ignored.
`q` is used only when type is AF_NORM_MATRIX_L_PQ; otherwise ignored.

functions.name: af::isLAPACKAvailable
functions.signature: AFAPI bool af::isLAPACKAvailable();
functions.description: Returns whether ArrayFire was compiled with LAPACK support.

functions.name: af_svd
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_svd(af_array *u, af_array *s, af_array *vt, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API for singular value decomposition. Produces U, singular values in `s` (diagonal), and V^H in `vt` from input `in`. Returns AF_SUCCESS on success or an af_err code on failure.
requirements: `u`, `s`, and `vt` must be non-null output pointers to receive resulting arrays.
`in` must be a valid af_array handle to a 2D matrix.
Caller must check the returned af_err for success.

functions.name: af_svd_inplace
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_svd_inplace(af_array *u, af_array *s, af_array *vt, af_array in);
functions.description: C API for in-place SVD. Minimizes memory by reusing storage from `in`. After the call, `in` contains random/undefined data. Returns AF_SUCCESS on success or an af_err code on failure.
requirements: `in` must represent a 2D matrix with dim0 >= dim1.
`u`, `s`, and `vt` must be non-null output pointers.
`in` will be modified; do not reuse its contents after the call.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_lu
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_lu(af_array *lower, af_array *upper, af_array *pivot, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API for LU decomposition. Computes L, U, and pivot indices from input matrix `in`. Returns AF_SUCCESS on success or an af_err code on failure.
requirements: `lower`, `upper`, and `pivot` must be non-null output pointers.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_lu_inplace
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_lu_inplace(af_array *pivot, af_array in, const bool is_lapack_piv);
functions.description: C API for in-place LU decomposition. Overwrites `in` with packed LU factors and writes permutation indices into `pivot`. Pivot format can be LAPACK-compliant. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `pivot` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle and will be overwritten with packed LU.
`is_lapack_piv` selects pivot format.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_qr
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_qr(af_array *q, af_array *r, af_array *tau, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API for QR decomposition. Returns orthogonal matrix Q, upper triangular R, and auxiliary vector tau from `in`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `q`, `r`, and `tau` must be non-null output pointers.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_qr_inplace
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_qr_inplace(af_array *tau, af_array in);
functions.description: C API for in-place QR decomposition. Overwrites `in` with packed QR representation; `tau` contains additional data. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `tau` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle and will be overwritten with packed QR.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_cholesky
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_cholesky(af_array *out, int *info, const af_array in, const bool is_upper);
functions.description: C API for Cholesky decomposition of a positive-definite matrix. Writes triangular factor to `out` (upper if `is_upper`, else lower). Writes 0 to `info` on success; otherwise writes the rank at which decomposition fails. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `in` must be a positive-definite matrix (af_array handle).
`out` and `info` must be non-null output pointers.
Caller must check both the returned af_err and the `info` value.
`is_upper` selects whether the output is upper or lower triangular.

functions.name: af_cholesky_inplace
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_cholesky_inplace(int *info, af_array in, const bool is_upper);
functions.description: C API for in-place Cholesky factorization. Overwrites `in` with the triangular factor. Sets `*info` to 0 on success or the failure rank otherwise. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `in` must be a positive-definite matrix (af_array handle) and will be overwritten.
`info` must be a non-null output pointer.
Caller must check both the returned af_err and the `info` value.
`is_upper` selects whether the stored factor is upper or lower triangular.

functions.name: af_solve
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_solve(af_array *x, const af_array a, const af_array b, const af_mat_prop options);
functions.description: C API to solve A x = B. Writes the solution matrix to `x`. `options` describes properties of `a` (e.g., triangular). Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `x` must be a non-null output pointer.
`a` and `b` must be valid af_array handles with compatible dimensions.
`options` must be one of AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_LOWER, or AF_MAT_UPPER.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_solve_lu
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_solve_lu(af_array *x, const af_array a, const af_array piv, const af_array b, const af_mat_prop options);
functions.description: C API to solve a system using a packed LU decomposition `a` and its pivot array `piv`. Writes solution to `x`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `x` must be a non-null output pointer.
`a` must be a packed LU decomposition of the coefficient matrix.
`piv` must be the pivot array corresponding to `a`.
`b` must be compatible dimensionally with the system.
`options` currently must be AF_MAT_NONE.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_inverse
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_inverse(af_array *out, const af_array in, const af_mat_prop options);
functions.description: C API to compute the inverse of `in`. Writes the inverse to `out`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `out` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array handle to an invertible square matrix (implied; not explicitly stated).
`options` currently must be AF_MAT_NONE.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_pinverse
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_pinverse(af_array *out, const af_array in, const double tol, const af_mat_prop options);
functions.description: C API to compute the Moore–Penrose pseudo-inverse of `in` using an SVD-based method. `tol` influences the singular value thresholding. Writes result to `out`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `out` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle.
`tol` defines the lower threshold used for singular values in the pseudo-inverse computation.
`options` must be AF_MAT_NONE.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_rank
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_rank(unsigned *rank, const af_array in, const double tol);
functions.description: C API to compute the numerical rank of matrix `in` with tolerance `tol`. Writes the rank to `*rank`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `rank` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle.
`tol` is a tolerance value used in rank determination.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_det
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_det(double *det_real, double *det_imag, const af_array in);
functions.description: C API to compute the determinant of `in`. Writes the real and imaginary parts to `det_real` and `det_imag`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `det_real` and `det_imag` must be non-null output pointers.
`in` must be a valid af_array matrix handle.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_norm
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_norm(double *out, const af_array in, const af_norm_type type, const double p, const double q);
functions.description: C API to compute a norm of `in`. The norm type is specified by `type`. Parameters `p` and `q` are used for P-norms and L_pq matrix norms as applicable. Writes the result to `*out`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code.
requirements: `out` must be a non-null output pointer.
`in` must be a valid af_array handle.
`type` must be a valid af_norm_type value.
`p` is used only when type is AF_NORM_VECTOR_P or AF_NORM_MATRIX_L_PQ; otherwise ignored.
`q` is used only when type is AF_NORM_MATRIX_L_PQ; otherwise ignored.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: af_is_lapack_available
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_is_lapack_available(bool *out);
functions.description: C API that reports whether ArrayFire was compiled with LAPACK support. Writes true/false to `*out`. Returns AF_SUCCESS or an error code (independent of `out`).
requirements: `out` must be a non-null output pointer.
Caller must check the returned af_err.

functions.name: printf
functions.signature: int printf(const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Writes formatted output to the standard output stream using a printf-style format string and corresponding variadic arguments. Commonly used inside this header’s macros (e.g., AF_MSG, AF_MEM_INFO) to print status lines.
requirements: format must be a valid C printf-style format string.
The number and types of variadic arguments must exactly match the conversion specifiers in format.
Return value should be checked: a negative value indicates an output error.
Thread-safety and locale effects are implementation-defined; avoid sharing FILE state unsafely across threads if applicable.

functions.name: fprintf
functions.signature: int fprintf(FILE *stream, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: Writes formatted output to the specified file stream using a printf-style format string and corresponding variadic arguments. Used in this header to print errors to stderr when af_device_mem_info fails.
requirements: stream must be a valid, non-null FILE* opened for writing (or update).
format must be a valid C printf-style format string.
The number and types of variadic arguments must exactly match the conversion specifiers in format.
Return value should be checked: a negative value indicates an output or stream error.
The stream’s buffering and thread-safety are implementation-defined; avoid data races on stream.

functions.name: af_device_mem_info
functions.signature: af_err af_device_mem_info(size_t *allocated_bytes, size_t *allocated_buffers, size_t *locked_bytes, size_t *locked_buffers);
functions.description: Queries ArrayFire’s device memory manager for current allocation and usage statistics, writing the counts of bytes and buffers both allocated in total and currently locked (in use). Intended usage is to pass four pointers to size_t that receive the results and then check the returned af_err for AF_SUCCESS before using the values (as demonstrated in AF_MEM_INFO).
requirements: allocated_bytes must be a valid, non-null pointer to size_t to receive the total allocated bytes.
allocated_buffers must be a valid, non-null pointer to size_t to receive the total allocated buffers.
locked_bytes must be a valid, non-null pointer to size_t to receive the in-use (locked) bytes.
locked_buffers must be a valid, non-null pointer to size_t to receive the in-use (locked) buffers.
Caller must check the return value: AF_SUCCESS indicates success; any other af_err is a failure and output values should not be used.
Must be called in a context where the ArrayFire device/memory manager is initialized; otherwise an error may be returned.

functions.name: af_create_memory_manager
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_create_memory_manager(af_memory_manager* out);
functions.description: Creates a new af_memory_manager handle with no attached function pointers. Use this before configuring function callbacks and installing it into ArrayFire.
requirements: AF_API_VERSION must be >= 37 (as this API is conditionally available).
out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the created handle.
Caller is responsible for eventually destroying the handle via af_release_memory_manager or by unsetting if installed.

functions.name: af_release_memory_manager
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_release_memory_manager(af_memory_manager handle);
functions.description: Destroys an af_memory_manager handle. This does not invoke the memory manager’s shutdown callback; it only frees the handle.
requirements: handle must be a valid af_memory_manager previously created (for example by af_create_memory_manager).

This call does NOT call the configured af_memory_manager_shutdown_fn; if shutdown semantics are required, the caller must ensure they were invoked via unset APIs or by calling the callback through other means before releasing.

functions.name: af_set_memory_manager
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_set_memory_manager(af_memory_manager handle);
functions.description: Registers the given memory manager as the default for non-pinned allocations in ArrayFire. It does not shut down or release any existing memory manager or free any associated memory.

functions.name: af::convolve2GradientNN
functions.signature:
AFAPI af::array af::convolve2GradientNN(const af::array& incoming_gradient,
                                         const af::array& original_signal,
                                         const af::array& original_filter,
                                         const af::array& convolved_output,
                                         const af::dim4 stride,
                                         const af::dim4 padding,
                                         const af::dim4 dilation,
                                         af::convGradientType grad_type);
functions.description: Computes the backward-pass gradient for 2D convolution (machine-learning convention) from a forward pass performed by af::convolve2NN. Depending on grad_type, returns the gradient with respect to the input signal or the filter (and possibly other supported targets). Typical use is during neural-network backpropagation: provide the upstream/incoming gradient, the original forward-pass signal and filter, the forward-pass output, and the original stride/padding/dilation used. Note: pass both dim0 and dim1 in the dim4 stride/padding/dilation; dimensions 2 and 3 are currently ignored.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 37 at compile time.
incoming_gradient must represent the upstream gradient to be distributed through the convolution backward pass (shape-compatible with the forward output). [inferred from description]
original_signal must be the input used in the corresponding forward 2D convolution; its assumed structure is (d0 x d1 x d2 x N).
original_filter must be the filter used in the corresponding forward 2D convolution; its assumed structure is (d0 x d1 x d2 x N).
convolved_output must be the output produced by the corresponding forward 2D convolution.
stride, padding, and dilation must specify the same values used in the forward pass. Provide dim0 and dim1; dimensions 2 and 3 are ignored.
grad_type selects which gradient to return; caller must choose a value supported by af::convGradientType.
All af::array and af::dim4 arguments must be valid and initialized ArrayFire objects. [inferred from types]

functions.name: af_convolve2_gradient_nn
functions.description: C API to compute the backward-pass gradient for 2D convolution (machine-learning convention) corresponding to af::convolve2NN. Writes to out the gradient specified by grad_type, given the upstream/incoming gradient, the original forward-pass signal and filter, the forward-pass output, and the original stride/padding/dilation.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 37 at compile time.
out must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the resulting af_array handle; on success the function returns AF_SUCCESS.
incoming_gradient must be the upstream gradient compatible with the forward output. [inferred from description]
original_signal must be the input used in the corresponding forward 2D convolution; assumed structure is (d0 x d1 x d2 x N).
original_filter must be the filter used in the corresponding forward 2D convolution; assumed structure is (d0 x d1 x d2 x N).
convolved_output must be the output produced by the corresponding forward 2D convolution.
stride_dims, padding_dims, and dilation_dims specify the number of dimensions; for 2D convolution these should be 2. [inferred from 2D operation]

strides must point to an array with at least stride_dims elements; paddings must point to an array with at least padding_dims elements; dilations must point to an array with at least dilation_dims elements; these must match the values used in the forward pass.
All af_array handles passed in must be valid (non-null) ArrayFire arrays. [inferred from types]
Caller must check the returned af_err and handle errors accordingly.

template<int rank>
array fftR2C(const array &in, const dim4& dims, const double norm_factor = 1.0);
functions.description: Computes a real-to-complex FFT of a real input along rank dimensions with optional padding dims and normalization. Returns only the non-redundant complex spectrum along the first transformed dimension.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
Template parameter rank: dimensionality of the transform.
in: real af::array.
dims: padded output dimensions before transform.
norm_factor: multiplicative normalization after transform.
Output first dimension size will be (dims[0] / 2) + 1; remaining dims unchanged.

functions.signature:
template<int rank>
array fftC2R(const array &in, bool is_odd = false, const double norm_factor = 1.0);
functions.description: Computes a complex-to-real inverse FFT from a spectrum containing only the non-redundant parts along rank dimensions. Controls final size parity with is_odd and applies normalization.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
Template parameter rank: dimensionality of the transform.
in: complex af::array containing only non-redundant parts of the signals.
is_odd: controls whether the reconstructed real size along the first dimension is odd.
norm_factor: multiplicative normalization after transform.
Output size: [2 * idim0 - 2 + is_odd, idim1, idim2, idim3], where idim* are input dimensions.

functions.description: C API: Real-to-complex FFT for 1D signals; outputs non-redundant spectrum with explicit normalization and optional padding to pad0.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out: output af_array pointer (complex).

functions.name: af::sparse
functions.signature: AFAPI array sparse(const dim_t nRows, const dim_t nCols, const array values, const array rowIdx, const array colIdx, const af::storage stype = AF_STORAGE_CSR);
functions.description: Creates a sparse af::array from separate af::array components containing nonzero values and their row and column indices, using the specified storage format. The function does not deep-copy the inputs; it creates references to them inside the sparse structure. Typical usage: assemble COO/CSR/CSC components and wrap them into a sparse array for computation.
requirements: nRows and nCols should be positive dimensions (inferred from matrix size semantics).
values, rowIdx, and colIdx must represent the same set of nonzero entries; their lengths must match (inferred from sparse triplet semantics; not explicitly stated).
Row and column indices must be within [0, nRows) and [0, nCols) respectively (inferred).
stype must be a valid af::storage value (e.g., AF_STORAGE_CSR/CSC/COO).
Inputs must be af::array objects that are initialized and compatible with the active backend.
Caller should be aware inputs are referenced (no deep copy); modifying/destroying them may affect the sparse array (explicit note).

functions.name: af::sparse
functions.signature: AFAPI array sparse(const dim_t nRows, const dim_t nCols, const dim_t nNZ, const void* const values, const int * const rowIdx, const int * const colIdx, const dtype type = f32, const af::storage stype = AF_STORAGE_CSR, const af::source src = afHost);
functions.description: Creates a device sparse af::array from host or device pointers providing the nonzero values and their row and column indices. The copy/reference rules follow those of constructing a regular af::array. Intended for building sparse matrices directly from raw buffers.
requirements: nRows and nCols should be positive (inferred).
nNZ is the number of nonzero entries and must be >= 0 (inferred).
values must point to at least nNZ elements of the specified dtype; type specifies the element type of values.
rowIdx and colIdx must each point to at least nNZ 32-bit integers representing row and column indices.
When src == afHost, pointers must be valid, readable host memory; when src == afDevice, pointers must be valid device memory for the current backend (explicit in comments).
Row and column indices must lie within [0, nRows) and [0, nCols) respectively (inferred).
stype must be a valid af::storage value (CSR/CSC/COO).
Pointers must be non-null when nNZ > 0 (inferred).

functions.description: Multiply two matrices with optional per-operand transpose/conjugate options. Intended for dense-dense matmul; also supports sparse–dense when the sparse input is the left-hand side in CSR format. Not supported inside GFOR. Usage: result = af::matmul(A, B, optLhs, optRhs).
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid af::array objects (initialized).
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for multiplication after applying optLhs/optRhs (inner dimensions must match).
optLhs must be one of AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_TRANS, AF_MAT_CTRANS.
optRhs must be one of AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_TRANS, AF_MAT_CTRANS.

Sparse–dense usage constraints: only one sparse input is supported and it must be lhs; rhs must be dense; the sparse array must be AF_STORAGE_CSR; the returned array is dense; when using sparse–dense, optRhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE and optLhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_TRANS, or AF_MAT_CTRANS.
Do not call from within GFOR.
