functions.description: Multiply two matrices, transposing the right-hand side internally. Equivalent to lhs * transpose(rhs). Not supported inside GFOR.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid af::array objects (initialized).
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for lhs * transpose(rhs).
Do not call from within GFOR.

functions.name: af::matmulTN
functions.signature: af::array af::matmulTN(const af::array &lhs, const af::array &rhs)
functions.description: Multiply two matrices, transposing the left-hand side internally. Equivalent to transpose(lhs) * rhs. Not supported inside GFOR.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid af::array objects (initialized).
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for transpose(lhs) * rhs.
Do not call from within GFOR.

functions.name: af::matmulTT
functions.signature: af::array af::matmulTT(const af::array &lhs, const af::array &rhs)
functions.description: Multiply two matrices, transposing both operands internally. Equivalent to transpose(lhs) * transpose(rhs). Not supported inside GFOR.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid af::array objects (initialized).
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for transpose(lhs) * transpose(rhs).
Do not call from within GFOR.

functions.name: af::dot
functions.signature: template <typename T> T af::dot(const af::array &lhs, const af::array &rhs, const af::matProp optLhs = AF_MAT_NONE, const af::matProp optRhs = AF_MAT_NONE)
functions.description: Compute a scalar dot (inner) product of two vectors and return the result on the host as type T. Conjugation options control whether either input is conjugated before multiplication. Not supported inside GFOR.
requirements: lhs and rhs must be valid af::array objects (initialized).
Inputs are vectors for a scalar dot product; their lengths must match.
optLhs and optRhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE or AF_MAT_CONJ.
Caller must choose T compatible with the input types; result is returned on host.

functions.name: af::transpose
functions.signature: af::array af::transpose(const af::array &in, const bool conjugate = false)
functions.description: Return the transpose of the input matrix. If conjugate is true, performs conjugate transpose (Hermitian).
requirements: in must be a valid af::array (initialized).
If conjugate is true, input should be of a complex-capable type to have an effect (otherwise it behaves as regular transpose).

functions.name: af::transposeInPlace
functions.signature: void af::transposeInPlace(af::array &in, const bool conjugate = false)
functions.description: Transpose the input matrix in place. If conjugate is true, performs conjugate transpose. Modifies the provided array.
requirements: in must be a valid, mutable af::array (initialized).
If conjugate is true, input should be of a complex-capable type to have an effect (otherwise it behaves as regular transpose).

functions.name: af_gemm
functions.signature: af_err af_gemm(af_array *C, const af_mat_prop opA, const af_mat_prop opB, const void *alpha, const af_array A, const af_array B, const void *beta)
functions.description: C interface to BLAS GEMM on af_array objects: computes C = alpha * opA(A) * opB(B) + beta * C. Supports batched GEMM when A or B have >2 dims (single alpha and beta used for all batches). The C handle can be null to allocate or a valid preallocated array to overwrite. See notes for s8 CUDA support.
requirements: C may be a null af_array handle to allocate output, or a valid af_array with correct type and shape to be overwritten.
A and B must be valid af_array handles; their element types must match each other and alpha/beta types (except s8 CUDA case).
opA/opB specify operations applied before multiplication; per docs these are either AF_MAT_NONE (noop) or AF_MAT_TRANS (transpose).
alpha and beta must be pointers to scalars of the same type as A and B (for general case).
For batched GEMM (A or B with >2 dims), only one alpha and one beta are used for all batch operations.
Passing an af_array that has not been initialized for C causes undefined behavior.
CUDA s8 support: when A and B are s8 on CUDA backend (v3.10.0+), alpha and beta must be f32, and output C will be f32; requires CUDA >= 10 and device compute capability >= 5.0.
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for multiplication after applying opA/opB.

functions.name: af_matmul
functions.signature: af_err af_matmul(af_array *out, const af_array lhs, const af_array rhs, const af_mat_prop optLhs, const af_mat_prop optRhs)
functions.description: C interface to matrix-multiply two arrays. When one operand is sparse, only lhs may be sparse (CSR) and the result is dense.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer; if *out is null, the function will allocate the result.
lhs and rhs must be valid af_array handles.
Matrix dimensions must be compatible for multiplication after applying optLhs/optRhs.

Sparse–dense constraints: only one sparse input supported and it must be lhs; rhs must be dense; lhs must be AF_STORAGE_CSR; output is dense; in sparse–dense, optLhs can be AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_TRANS, AF_MAT_CTRANS; optRhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE.

optLhs must be one of AF_MAT_NONE, AF_MAT_TRANS, AF_MAT_CTRANS; optRhs must be one of AF_MAT_NONE (and possibly AF_MAT_TRANS/CTRANS for dense-dense as per API, but only AF_MAT_NONE when sparse–dense).

functions.name: af_dot
functions.signature: af_err af_dot(af_array *out, const af_array lhs, const af_array rhs, const af_mat_prop optLhs, const af_mat_prop optRhs)
functions.description: C interface to compute the scalar dot (inner) product of two vectors, returning the result as a 1-element af_array.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer; if *out is null, the function will allocate the scalar result.
lhs and rhs must be valid af_array handles.
Inputs should be vectors for a scalar dot product; their lengths must match.
optLhs and optRhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE or AF_MAT_CONJ.

functions.name: af_dot_all
functions.signature: af_err af_dot_all(double *real, double *imag, const af_array lhs, const af_array rhs, const af_mat_prop optLhs, const af_mat_prop optRhs)
functions.description: C interface to compute the scalar dot (inner) product of two vectors and return the result as host scalars in real and imag. Suitable for real and complex data; for real types, imag will be zero.
requirements: real and imag must be valid, writable pointers to host doubles.
lhs and rhs must be valid af_array handles.
Inputs should be vectors for a scalar dot product; their lengths must match.
optLhs and optRhs can only be AF_MAT_NONE or AF_MAT_CONJ.

functions.name: af_transpose
functions.signature: af_err af_transpose(af_array *out, af_array in, const bool conjugate)
functions.description: C interface to return the transpose (or conjugate transpose when conjugate=true) of the input matrix.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer; if *out is null, the function will allocate the result.
in must be a valid af_array handle.
If conjugate is true, input should be of a complex-capable type to have an effect (otherwise it behaves as regular transpose).

functions.name: af_transpose_inplace
functions.signature: af_err af_transpose_inplace(af_array in, const bool conjugate)
functions.description: C interface to transpose an array in place. If conjugate is true, performs conjugate transpose. Modifies the provided array.
requirements: in must be a valid, mutable af_array handle.
If conjugate is true, input should be of a complex-capable type to have an effect (otherwise it behaves as regular transpose).

functions.name: af::fast
functions.signature: AFAPI features fast(const array& in, const float thr=20.0f, const unsigned arc_length=9, const bool non_max=true, const float feature_ratio=0.05f, const unsigned edge=3);
functions.description: Detect FAST keypoints in a single-channel (grayscale) image. Returns an af::features object with x/y coordinates and score; orientation is 0 and size is 1 because FAST does not compute them. Typical usage: pass a grayscale af::array image; control threshold and arc length; optionally enable non-max suppression; limit detections via feature_ratio and discard a border of width edge.
requirements: in must be a grayscale (single-channel) image; color images are not supported.
arc_length must be within [9-16].
edge must be >= 3 (the FAST circle radius).
If too many features are detected, those beyond feature_ratio * in.elements() are discarded (not score-based).

functions.name: af::harris
functions.signature: AFAPI features harris(const array& in, const unsigned max_corners=500, const float min_response=1e5f, const float sigma=1.f, const unsigned block_size=0, const float k_thr=0.04f);
functions.description: Compute Harris corners on a grayscale image and return strongest responses as an af::features object (x, y, score). Orientation is 0 and size is 1. Use max_corners to cap returned features or set it to 0 to use min_response. Neighborhood can be circular (controlled by sigma) or square (block_size).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
If block_size == 0, sigma is used and must be >= 0.5f and <= 5.0f.
If block_size != 0, block_size must be >= 3 and <= 31.
k_thr (Harris constant) must be >= 0.01f.
If max_corners = 0, min_response is used to retain corners.

functions.name: af::orb
functions.signature: AFAPI void orb(features& feat, array& desc, const array& image, const float fast_thr=20.f, const unsigned max_feat=400, const float scl_fctr=1.5f, const unsigned levels=4, const bool blur_img=false);
functions.description: Detect ORB keypoints and compute their binary descriptors. Outputs an af::features object and an Nx8 descriptor array (each descriptor is 8 32-bit values for 256 bits). Controls include FAST threshold, a cap on features kept, image pyramid scale factor and levels, and optional Gaussian pre-blur.
requirements: image must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
desc is output as an Nx8 array where N is the number of selected features.
feat and desc are output parameters and will be overwritten.

functions.name: af::sift
functions.signature: AFAPI void sift(features& feat, array& desc, const array& in, const unsigned n_layers=3, const float contrast_thr=0.04f, const float edge_thr=10.f, const float init_sigma=1.6f, const bool double_input=true, const float intensity_scale=0.00390625f, const float feature_ratio=0.05f);
functions.description: Run SIFT keypoint detector and 128D descriptor extractor on a grayscale image. Outputs detected features and an Nx128 descriptor matrix. Parameters control octave layers, contrast/edge thresholds, initial blur, optional image doubling, intensity scaling, and a cap on total features via feature_ratio.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
desc is output as an Nx128 array where N is the number of SIFT features.
double_input, intensity_scale, and feature_ratio affect algorithm behavior as documented; features detected after feature_ratio * in.elements() are discarded.

functions.name: af::gloh
functions.signature: AFAPI void gloh(features& feat, array& desc, const array& in, const unsigned n_layers=3, const float contrast_thr=0.04f, const float edge_thr=10.f, const float init_sigma=1.6f, const bool double_input=true, const float intensity_scale=0.00390625f, const float feature_ratio=0.05f);
functions.description: Run SIFT detector with GLOH descriptor extraction. Outputs features and an Nx272 descriptor matrix. Parameters mirror SIFT, including octave layers, thresholds, initial sigma, optional input doubling, intensity scaling, and feature cap via feature_ratio.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
desc is output as an Nx272 array where N is the number of detected features.
Features detected after feature_ratio * in.elements() are discarded.

functions.name: af::hammingMatcher
functions.signature: AFAPI void hammingMatcher(array& idx, array& dist, const array& query, const array& train, const dim_t dist_dim=0, const unsigned n_dist=1);
functions.description: Find nearest neighbors between query and train sets using Hamming distance (intended for binary descriptors). Outputs indices and distances of the n_dist closest matches per query along the chosen dimension. This is a convenience wrapper equivalent to nearestNeighbour(..., AF_SHD).
requirements: dist_dim indicates the dimension analyzed for distance and must be of equal length for both query and train along that dimension.
n_dist must be <= 256.
idx and dist are MxN outputs where M is the number of queries and N is n_dist, populated with indices and Hamming distances respectively.

functions.name: af::nearestNeighbour
functions.signature: AFAPI void nearestNeighbour(array& idx, array& dist, const array& query, const array& train, const dim_t dist_dim=0, const unsigned n_dist=1, const af_match_type dist_type = AF_SSD);
functions.description: General k-NN search between query and train point sets using a chosen distance metric (SAD, SSD, or Hamming). Points are laid out with coordinates along one dimension and samples along the other, determined by dist_dim. Returns indices and distances of the n_dist nearest neighbors for each query.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
query and train must describe point coordinates along dim0 and list samples along dim1 if dist_dim==0, or vice versa if dist_dim==1.
query and train must use the same coordinate dimension specified by dist_dim (equal length along that dimension).
n_dist must be <= 256.
dist_type must be one of AF_SAD, AF_SSD, or AF_SHD.

functions.name: af::matchTemplate
functions.signature: AFAPI array matchTemplate(const array &searchImg, const array &templateImg, const matchType mType=AF_SAD);
functions.description: Compute template matching between searchImg and templateImg using the specified disparity metric and return a response map of disparities for each valid window position. Supports batch operation when searchImg is 3D.
requirements: mType must be one of the values defined by af_match_type (e.g., AF_SAD, AF_SSD, AF_ZNCC, depending on library).
If searchImg is a 3D array, a batch operation will be performed.

functions.name: af::susan
functions.signature: AFAPI features susan(const array& in, const unsigned radius=3, const float diff_thr=32.0f, const float geom_thr=10.0f, const float feature_ratio=0.05f, const unsigned edge=3);
functions.description: Detect corners using the SUSAN algorithm on a grayscale/intensity image. Returns detected features (coordinates, score, orientation, size). Supports batched operation for 3D inputs. May throw on failure.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
in must be a grayscale/intensity image.
feature_ratio limits the maximum number of features returned.
edge indicates the border width to skip for detection.
If in is a 3D array, a batch operation will be performed.

functions.name: af::dog
functions.signature: AFAPI array dog(const array& in, const int radius1, const int radius2);
functions.description: Compute the Difference of Gaussians by smoothing the input image with two Gaussian kernels (radii radius1 and radius2) and returning their difference.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
in is an input image; radius1 and radius2 specify the radii of the two Gaussian kernels.

functions.name: af::homography
functions.signature: AFAPI void homography(array& H, int& inliers, const array& x_src, const array& y_src, const array& x_dst, const array& y_dst, const af_homography_type htype=AF_HOMOGRAPHY_RANSAC, const float inlier_thr=3.f, const unsigned iterations=1000, const dtype otype=f32);
functions.description: Estimate a 3x3 homography H from corresponding point coordinates using either RANSAC or LMedS. Outputs the homography and the estimated number of inliers. RANSAC uses inlier_thr as the maximum L2 distance and iterations as the iteration budget (interpretation depends on backend).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
H is output as a 3x3 array of type otype.
inliers is an output indicating the estimated number of inliers; larger inlier_thr generally increases inliers for RANSAC.
htype must be AF_HOMOGRAPHY_RANSAC or AF_HOMOGRAPHY_LMEDS.
If backend is CPU, iterations is the maximum number of iterations; on CUDA/OpenCL, iterations is the total number of random 4-point trials.
x_src, y_src, x_dst, y_dst are arrays of source and destination point coordinates.

functions.name: af_fast
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_fast(af_features *out, const af_array in, const float thr, const unsigned arc_length, const bool non_max, const float feature_ratio, const unsigned edge);
functions.description: C API for FAST keypoint detection on a grayscale image. Produces an af_features handle with x/y/score; orientation is 0 and size is 1. Controls include threshold, arc length, optional non-max suppression, feature cap via feature_ratio, and border exclusion via edge.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the resulting af_features.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
arc_length must be within [9-16].
edge must be >= 3.
On success returns AF_SUCCESS; otherwise an appropriate af_err is returned.

functions.name: af_harris
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_harris(af_features *out, const af_array in, const unsigned max_corners, const float min_response, const float sigma, const unsigned block_size, const float k_thr);
functions.description: C API for Harris corner detection. Returns strongest corners in an af_features handle with score as Harris response; orientation is 0 and size is 1.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid pointer to receive af_features.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
If block_size == 0, sigma must be >= 0.5f and <= 5.0f.
If block_size != 0, block_size must be >= 3 and <= 31.
k_thr must be >= 0.01f.
If max_corners = 0, min_response is used to retain corners.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_orb
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_orb(af_features *feat, af_array *desc, const af_array in, const float fast_thr, const unsigned max_feat, const float scl_fctr, const unsigned levels, const bool blur_img);
functions.description: C API for ORB detection and binary descriptor extraction on a grayscale image. Outputs af_features and an Nx8 descriptor array.
requirements: feat must be a valid pointer to receive af_features.
desc must be a valid pointer to receive the Nx8 descriptor array.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_sift
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_sift(af_features *feat, af_array *desc, const af_array in, const unsigned n_layers, const float contrast_thr, const float edge_thr, const float init_sigma, const bool double_input, const float intensity_scale, const float feature_ratio);
functions.description: C API for SIFT feature detection and 128D descriptor extraction on a grayscale image. Outputs features and an Nx128 descriptor array.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
feat must be a valid pointer to receive af_features.
desc must be a valid pointer to receive the Nx128 descriptor array.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
Features detected after feature_ratio * in.elements() are discarded.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_gloh
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_gloh(af_features *feat, af_array *desc, const af_array in, const unsigned n_layers, const float contrast_thr, const float edge_thr, const float init_sigma, const bool double_input, const float intensity_scale, const float feature_ratio);
functions.description: C API for SIFT detector with GLOH descriptor (272D). Outputs features and an Nx272 descriptor array.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
feat must be a valid pointer to receive af_features.
desc must be a valid pointer to receive the Nx272 descriptor array.
in must be a grayscale image; color images are not supported.
Features detected after feature_ratio * in.elements() are discarded.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_hamming_matcher
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_hamming_matcher(af_array* idx, af_array* dist, const af_array query, const af_array train, const dim_t dist_dim, const unsigned n_dist);
functions.description: C API wrapper that finds nearest neighbors using Hamming distance between query and train sets. Returns indices and distances of the n_dist smallest Hamming distances per query.
requirements: idx and dist must be valid pointers to receive MxN outputs (M = number of queries, N = n_dist).
dist_dim indicates the coordinate dimension and must be of equal length for both query and train along that dimension.
n_dist must be <= 256.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_nearest_neighbour
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_nearest_neighbour(af_array* idx, af_array* dist, const af_array query, const af_array train, const dim_t dist_dim, const unsigned n_dist, const af_match_type dist_type);
functions.description: C API for general nearest-neighbor search using SAD, SSD, or Hamming distance. Returns indices and distances for the n_dist nearest neighbors per query.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
idx and dist must be valid pointers to receive outputs of size MxN (M = n_dist, N = number of queries).
query and train must describe coordinates along dim0 and list samples along dim1 if dist_dim == 0, or vice versa if dist_dim == 1.
query and train must both use the same coordinate dimension indicated by dist_dim (equal length along that dimension).
n_dist must be <= 256.
dist_type must be AF_SAD, AF_SSD, or AF_SHD.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_match_template
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_match_template(af_array *out, const af_array search_img, const af_array template_img, const af_match_type m_type);
functions.description: C API for image template matching. Computes a disparity/response map between search_img and template_img using the specified metric and writes it to out. Supports batched operation when search_img is 3D.
requirements: out must be a valid pointer to receive the output disparity array.
m_type must be a valid af_match_type value.
If search_img is a 3D array, a batch operation will be performed.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_susan
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_susan(af_features* out, const af_array in, const unsigned radius, const float diff_thr, const float geom_thr, const float feature_ratio, const unsigned edge);
functions.description: C API for SUSAN corner detection on a grayscale/intensity image. Produces an af_features handle of detected features. Supports batched 3D inputs.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid pointer to receive af_features.
in must be a grayscale/intensity image.
feature_ratio limits the maximum number of features returned.
edge indicates how many pixels of border to skip.
If in is a 3D array, a batch operation will be performed.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_dog
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_dog(af_array *out, const af_array in, const int radius1, const int radius2);
functions.description: C API wrapper to compute Difference of Gaussians: smooth input with two Gaussian kernels (radius1, radius2) and output their difference.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31.
out must be a valid pointer to receive the output array.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: af_homography
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err af_homography(af_array *H, int *inliers, const af_array x_src, const af_array y_src, const af_array x_dst, const af_array y_dst, const af_homography_type htype, const float inlier_thr, const unsigned iterations, const af_dtype otype);
functions.description: C API to estimate a 3x3 homography matrix from point correspondences using RANSAC or LMedS. Outputs the homography matrix and the estimated number of inliers. RANSAC uses inlier_thr as the inlier distance threshold and iterations as the iteration budget (backend-dependent semantics).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32.
H must be a valid pointer to receive a 3x3 array of type otype.
inliers must be a valid pointer to receive the inlier count.
htype must be AF_HOMOGRAPHY_RANSAC or AF_HOMOGRAPHY_LMEDS.
If backend is CPU, iterations is the maximum number of iterations; if CUDA/OpenCL, iterations is the total number of random 4-point trials.
x_src, y_src, x_dst, y_dst provide source/destination point coordinates.
Returns AF_SUCCESS on success; otherwise an af_err code.

functions.name: afoneapi::array
functions.signature: af::array afoneapi::array(af::dim4 idims, cl_mem buf, af::dtype type, bool retain = false)
functions.description: Creates an af::array that wraps an existing OpenCL cl_mem buffer with the given dimensions and data type. It queries the buffer’s cl_context and verifies it matches ArrayFire’s current context; on mismatch it throws an af::exception. If retain is true, the function calls clRetainMemObject on buf before wrapping it. Intended for interop workflows where a pre-existing OpenCL buffer needs to be used as an ArrayFire array.
requirements: buf must be a valid OpenCL cl_mem object.
The cl_context associated with buf must be identical to ArrayFire’s current context; otherwise the function throws.
type should describe the actual element type stored in buf; mismatch can lead to incorrect behavior (not validated here).
idims must describe the intended shape; its total element count should be compatible with the underlying buffer size (not validated here).
If retain is true, the OpenCL runtime must be available to successfully retain the buffer; ArrayFire will throw on failure.
This function may throw af::exception on errors (context mismatch, OpenCL query/retain failure, or ArrayFire device array creation failure).

functions.name: afoneapi::getDeviceType
functions.signature: afoneapi::deviceType afoneapi::getDeviceType()
functions.description: Returns an enumeration describing the type of the current device used by ArrayFire. On failure it throws an af::exception.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 39 for this symbol to be available.
There must be a current ArrayFire device; the function may throw af::exception if querying the device type fails.

functions.name: afoneapi::getPlatform
functions.signature: afoneapi::platform afoneapi::getPlatform()
functions.description: Returns a vendor/platform enumeration for the current device’s platform. On failure it throws an af::exception.
requirements: Requires AF_API_VERSION >= 39 for this symbol to be available.
There must be a current ArrayFire device/platform; the function may throw af::exception if querying the platform fails.

functions.name: afcu_get_stream
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err afcu_get_stream(cudaStream_t* stream, int id);
functions.description: Returns, via output parameter, the CUDA stream used by the CUDA device with the given ArrayFire device id in the current ArrayFire context. Use this to interoperate with native CUDA code on a specific ArrayFire-managed device.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31 and the CUDA backend is present.
stream must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the CUDA stream.
id must be a valid ArrayFire device id corresponding to a CUDA device in the current ArrayFire context.
Caller must check the returned af_err and handle errors (AF_SUCCESS indicates success).

functions.name: afcu_get_native_id
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err afcu_get_native_id(int* nativeid, int id);
functions.description: Retrieves, via output parameter, the native CUDA device id (as used by CUDA runtime) for the CUDA device addressed by the given ArrayFire device id. Useful for mapping ArrayFire device indices to CUDA’s native device numbering.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31 and the CUDA backend is present.
nativeid must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the native CUDA device id.
id must be a valid ArrayFire device id corresponding to a CUDA device in the current ArrayFire context.
Caller must check the returned af_err and handle errors (AF_SUCCESS indicates success).

functions.name: afcu_set_native_id
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err afcu_set_native_id(int nativeid);
functions.description: Sets the active ArrayFire CUDA device by specifying the native CUDA device id. This switches ArrayFire’s active device to the given CUDA device.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32 and the CUDA backend is present.
nativeid must correspond to a valid CUDA device present in the system.
Switching devices may affect subsequent ArrayFire operations that depend on the active device; caller must check the returned af_err and handle errors (AF_SUCCESS indicates success).

functions.name: afcu_cublasSetMathMode
functions.signature: AFAPI af_err afcu_cublasSetMathMode(cublasMath_t mode);
functions.description: Sets the cuBLAS math mode on ArrayFire’s internal cuBLAS handle. Refer to cuBLAS documentation for effects of different modes (e.g., default vs tensor op math).
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 37 and the CUDA/cuBLAS backend is present.
mode must be a valid cublasMath_t value (e.g., CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH, CUBLAS_TENSOR_OP_MATH).
Caller must check the returned af_err and handle errors (AF_SUCCESS indicates success).

functions.name: afcu::getStream
functions.signature: static inline cudaStream_t afcu::getStream(int id);
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper that returns the CUDA stream used by the CUDA device identified by the given ArrayFire device id. Internally calls afcu_get_stream and throws on failure.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31 and the CUDA backend is present.
id must be a valid ArrayFire device id corresponding to a CUDA device in the current ArrayFire context.
On error, this function throws af::exception; callers must be prepared to catch exceptions.

functions.name: afcu::getNativeId
functions.signature: static inline int afcu::getNativeId(int id);
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper that returns the native CUDA device id for the CUDA device referenced by the given ArrayFire device id. Internally calls afcu_get_native_id and throws on failure.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 31 and the CUDA backend is present.
id must be a valid ArrayFire device id corresponding to a CUDA device in the current ArrayFire context.
On error, this function throws af::exception; callers must be prepared to catch exceptions.

functions.name: afcu::setNativeId
functions.signature: static inline void afcu::setNativeId(int nativeId);
functions.description: C++ convenience wrapper that sets the active ArrayFire CUDA device using the native CUDA device id. Internally calls afcu_set_native_id and throws on failure.
requirements: Available only when AF_API_VERSION >= 32 and the CUDA backend is present.
nativeId must correspond to a valid CUDA device present in the system.
On error, this function throws af::exception; callers must be prepared to catch exceptions.

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Target expects arbitrary raw bytes buffers that will be used as host memory to
# initialize or write ArrayFire arrays. The stubs compute sizes from dims, dtype,
# and cap input sizes up to small limits (<= 2048).
#
# Strategy
# - Generate buffers whose size is suitable for multiple stub paths:
#   * af_create_array: nbytes = elems * 4 (f32); elems up to 512 -> nbytes up to 2048
#   * af_write_array: nbytes depends on dtype and elems, but fuzz stub truncates/extends
#   * af::array::write: uses self->bytes() previously set by other fuzz flows
#   * createStridedArray / af_create_strided_array: buffer size arbitrary, but having
#     sizes that represent meaningful element patterns helps exercise code paths
# - Compose patterns: zeros, ramps, alternating bit patterns, random floats/ints,
#   IEEE specials (NaN/Inf), and small images-like tiles. Keep total size <= 2048.
# - Randomize selection based on seed, while always returning a valid bytes object.

MAX_BYTES = 2048


def _pack_f32_list(vals: List[float]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<' + 'f'*len(vals), *vals)


def _pack_f64_list(vals: List[float]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<' + 'd'*len(vals), *vals)


def _pack_i32_list(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<' + 'i'*len(vals), *vals)


def _pack_u8_list(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
    return bytes([v & 0xFF for v in vals])


def _make_pattern_bytes(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a base pattern kind
    kind = rng.choice([
        'zeros', 'ones', 'alt_ff00', 'alt_f00f', 'ramp_u8', 'ramp_i32',
        'rand_u8', 'rand_f32', 'special_f32', 'image_tile_u8', 'checker_u8',
        'rand_f64', 'rand_i32'
    ])

    data = b''

    if kind == 'zeros':
        data = bytes(target_size)

    elif kind == 'ones':
        data = bytes([1]) * target_size

    elif kind == 'alt_ff00':
        unit = b'\xFF\x00'
        reps = (target_size + 1) // 2
        data = (unit * reps)[:target_size]

    elif kind == 'alt_f00f':
        unit = b'\xF0\x0F'
        reps = (target_size + 1) // 2
        data = (unit * reps)[:target_size]

    elif kind == 'ramp_u8':
        start = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        step = rng.randrange(1, 17)
        vals = [(start + i*step) & 0xFF for i in range(target_size)]
        data = _pack_u8_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'ramp_i32':
        # Make length a multiple of 4
        n = target_size // 4
        if n == 0:
            n = 1
        start = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
        step = rng.randint(-7, 7) or 1
        vals = [start + i*step for i in range(n)]
        data = _pack_i32_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'rand_u8':
        data = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(target_size))

    elif kind == 'rand_f32':
        n = max(1, target_size // 4)
        vals = [rng.uniform(-1e3, 1e3) for _ in range(n)]
        data = _pack_f32_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'special_f32':
        # Mix of typical values and IEEE specials
        specials = [
            0.0, -0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1e-8, -1e-8, 1e8, -1e8,
            float('inf'), float('-inf'), float('nan')
        ]
        n = max(1, target_size // 4)
        vals = [rng.choice(specials) for _ in range(n)]
        data = _pack_f32_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'image_tile_u8':
        # Build a small WxH grayscale tile and flatten
        w = rng.choice([4, 8, 16, 32])
        h = rng.choice([4, 8, 16, 32])
        size = w * h
        # Gradient pattern
        vals = [int(255 * ((x / max(1, w-1)) * 0.5 + (y / max(1, h-1)) * 0.5))
                for y in range(h) for x in range(w)]
        data = _pack_u8_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'checker_u8':
        w = rng.choice([8, 16, 32])
        h = rng.choice([8, 16, 32])
        bw = rng.choice([1, 2, 4])
        vals = []
        for y in range(h):
            for x in range(w):
                v = 255 if ((x // bw + y // bw) % 2 == 0) else 0
                vals.append(v)
        data = _pack_u8_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'rand_f64':
        n = max(1, target_size // 8)
        vals = [rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6) for _ in range(n)]
        data = _pack_f64_list(vals)

    elif kind == 'rand_i32':
        n = max(1, target_size // 4)
        vals = [rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1) for _ in range(n)]
        data = _pack_i32_list(vals)

    # Resize to requested size: truncate or pad with zeros
    if len(data) < target_size:
        data = data + bytes(target_size - len(data))
    elif len(data) > target_size:
        data = data[:target_size]

    return data


def _compose_sections(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> bytes:
    # Compose multiple sections with different patterns to increase variety.
    # Ensure final size <= budget.
    remaining = budget
    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Decide how many chunks [1..4]
    num_chunks = rng.randint(1, 4)

    # Bias first chunk to element-size-friendly size (multiple of 4)
    for i in range(num_chunks):
        if remaining <= 0:
            break
        if i == num_chunks - 1:
            size = remaining
        else:
            # Allocate between 1/8 and 1/2 of remaining
            low = max(1, remaining // 8)
            high = max(low, remaining // 2)
            size = rng.randint(low, high)
        # For the first chunk, align to 4 to help f32 paths
        if i == 0 and size >= 4:
            size = (size // 4) * 4
            if size == 0:
                size = 4
        chunks.append(_make_pattern_bytes(rng, size))
        remaining -= size

    return b''.join(chunks)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose an overall size tailored to the stubs:
    # - Frequently choose multiples of 4 to match f32/i32
    # - Keep within [16, 2048]
    size_choices: List[int] = []
    # Multiples of 4 up to 2048
    size_choices += [4 * k for k in range(4, MAX_BYTES // 4 + 1)]
    # Some non-multiples to exercise u8 paths
    size_choices += [17, 31, 63, 127, 255, 511, 777, 1023, 1501]
    target_size = rng.choice(size_choices)
    target_size = min(MAX_BYTES, max(16, target_size))

    data = _compose_sections(rng, target_size)

    # As a final touch, optionally prepend or append small headers/footers of known values
    # that might land at offset 0 in strided creates.
    if rng.random() < 0.4 and len(data) + 16 <= MAX_BYTES:
        header = _make_pattern_bytes(rng, 16)
        data = header + data
    if rng.random() < 0.4 and len(data) + 16 <= MAX_BYTES:
        footer = _make_pattern_bytes(rng, 16)
        data = data + footer

    # Trim if exceeded due to optional header/footer
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]

    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: free-form text used for std::string / C strings and filenames.
# Target stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(). Our buffer will
# be split by the harness into multiple pulls. We'll pack multiple distinct
# strings sequentially so different calls get meaningful values: titles, keys,
# messages, printf formats/strings, and filenames. Keep bytes <= 4096.

SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

def _rand_words(rng: random.Random, min_words=1, max_words=8) -> str:
    words: List[str] = []
    n = rng.randint(min_words, max_words)
    for _ in range(n):
        wl = rng.randint(1, 12)
        # Mix alnum plus some punctuation that is safe in labels
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:+#@/"
        w = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(wl))
        words.append(w)
    return ' '.join(words)

def _rand_title(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    prefixes = ["Plot", "Image", "VectorField", "Debug", "Info", "Warning", "AF", "ArrayFire"]
    return f"{rng.choice(prefixes)}: {_rand_words(rng,1,4)}"

def _rand_label(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_words(rng, 2, 6)

def _rand_message(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choices = [
        "Memory usage report",
        "Device status",
        "Rendering cell",
        "Saving array",
        "Loading key",
        "Axes update",
        "Computation finished",
    ]
    return f"{rng.choice(choices)} :: {_rand_words(rng,1,5)}"

def _rand_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Keys for save/read; prefer simple tokens without spaces
    n = rng.randint(3, 12)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-:"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate likely-writable temp-like filenames; no directories to avoid path issues
    stems = ["af", "array", "data", "vec", "img", "tmp", "cache", "store"]
    ext_choices = [".af", ".bin", ".dat", ".ar", ".arr"]
    stem = rng.choice(stems)
    mid = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(3,10)))
    ext = rng.choice(ext_choices)
    name = f"{stem}_{mid}{ext}"
    # Ensure only safe chars
    name = ''.join(c if c in SAFE_FILENAME_CHARS else '_' for c in name)
    return name

def _rand_printf_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For stubs, formats are constant; but FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for labels/titles.
    # Provide benign strings that could also serve as printf data if used.
    s = _rand_words(rng, 1, 6)
    # Occasionally include percent signs but escape as %% to avoid format issues
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s = s + " %" * rng.randint(1,3)
        s = s.replace('%', '%%')
    return s

def _pick_colormap_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Title to accompany colormap; purely textual
    return rng.choice(["Default", "Inferno", "Magma", "Plasma", "Viridis", "Heat", "Blue"]) + " Map"

def _make_section(tag: str, content: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode a section with a header to help the consumer split, though the harness
    # will likely just consume bytes sequentially.
    # Format: [TAG]\nCONTENT\0
    return (f"[{tag}]\n{content}\0").encode('utf-8')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Provide a mix of strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 10)):
        parts.append(_make_section("MSG", _rand_message(rng)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        parts.append(_make_section("TITLE", _rand_title(rng)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)):
        parts.append(_make_section("LABEL", _rand_label(rng)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        parts.append(_make_section("PRINTF", _rand_printf_string(rng)))
    for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)):
        parts.append(_make_section("KEY", _rand_key(rng)))

    # Include some specific axis title-like strings
    parts.append(_make_section("XTITLE", "X-Axis"))
    parts.append(_make_section("YTITLE", "Y-Axis"))
    parts.append(_make_section("ZTITLE", "Z-Axis"))

    # Colormap label-like strings
    for _ in range(3):
        parts.append(_make_section("CMAP", _pick_colormap_name(rng)))

    # Filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        parts.append(_make_section("FILE", _rand_filename(rng)))

    # Ensure overall size <= 4096
    blob = b''.join(parts)
    return blob[:4096]

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Goal: Produce plausible, writable file paths (including directories and extensions)
# that the target stubs will use for saving/loading images and arrays. The fuzzer
# provides FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() which expects a path pointing to random fuzzable data.
# We will return a bytes buffer that the harness interprets as the content used to
# initialize its randomness and path choice. Since the harness just reads a buffer
# and then requests a filename string, we encode one or more newline-separated paths
# along with occasional keys/strings the stubs ask for via FUZZ_PARAM_STR(). The
# harness typically consumes bytes sequentially for each FUZZ_PARAM_* call.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit several candidate paths that are valid in most environments:
#   - Relative paths within a temp-like directory (./, ./subdir/, nested)
#   - Filenames with various extensions used by ArrayFire image IO (png, jpg, tiff, bmp, ppm, exr, hdr)
#   - Ensure directories look creatable (no absolute root requirements)
# - Also include a few random ASCII keys/strings for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers.
# - Keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness via input seed.
#
# Notes:
# - We avoid absolute paths to not depend on system layout. The harness typically writes
#   to the given path; relative paths in the working dir are usually fine.
# - Include some paths containing spaces, unicode, and long names to exercise code paths.

IMAGE_EXTS = ["png", "jpg", "jpeg", "tiff", "bmp", "ppm", "pgm", "exr", "hdr"]
ARRAY_EXTS = ["afarray", "arr", "bin", "dat"]

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"


def rand_name(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=12, extra_chars: str = "") -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS + extra_chars) for _ in range(n))
    # avoid trailing dots or spaces in names
    return base.strip(" .") or "file"


def rand_dirs(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts = []
    depth = r. randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        # add occasional unicode or space
        extra = "  " if r.random() < 0.2 else ""
        if r.random() < 0.2:
            extra += "μ"
        parts.append(rand_name(r, 2, 10, extra))
    return parts


def make_rel_path(r: random.Random, exts: List[str]) -> str:
    dirs = rand_dirs(r)
    prefix_choice = r.random()
    if prefix_choice < 0.5:
        prefix = "./"
    elif prefix_choice < 0.7:
        prefix = "./tmp/"
        dirs = ["tmp"] + dirs
    else:
        prefix = ""
    stem_extra = ""
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        stem_extra = " "  # space in filename
    if r.random() < 0.1:
        stem_extra += "μ"  # unicode char
    stem = rand_name(r, 3, 16, stem_extra)
    ext = r.choice(exts)
    path = "/".join(dirs + [f"{stem}.{ext}"]) if dirs else f"{stem}.{ext}"
    # normalize duplicate slashes while preserving leading ./
    full = (prefix + path).replace("//", "/")
    return full


def make_key(r: random.Random) -> str:
    length = r.randint(4, 24)
    alphabet = SAFE_CHARS + " _-.:/"
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length)).strip()
    return s or "key"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide how many filenames and keys to emit
    n_images = r.randint(3, 8)
    n_arrays = r.randint(2, 5)
    n_keys = r.randint(3, 7)

    lines: List[str] = []

    # Mix image-format filenames
    for _ in range(n_images):
        lines.append(make_rel_path(r, IMAGE_EXTS))

    # Mix array/other filenames used by saveArray/readArray
    for _ in range(n_arrays):
        # sometimes reuse image extensions to test image-native paths too
        if r.random() < 0.4:
            lines.append(make_rel_path(r, IMAGE_EXTS))
        else:
            lines.append(make_rel_path(r, ARRAY_EXTS))

    # Add some keys/strings that may be consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
    for _ in range(n_keys):
        lines.append(make_key(r))

    # Add a couple of known-good simple names at the end for fallback
    lines.extend([
        "./af_out.png",
        "./af_out.tiff",
        "./af_store.arr",
        "af space name.jpg",
        "key_default",
    ])

    # Shuffle lines to provide variety between calls
    r.shuffle(lines)

    # Join with newlines; ensure total size <= 4096
    blob = "\n".join(lines)
    b = blob.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Trim to last full line under limit
        b = b[:4096]
        # avoid cutting multibyte; back up to last newline
        nl = b.rfind(b"\n")
        if nl != -1:
            b = b[:nl]
    return b

import random
from typing import List

# Target data type: printf-style format string for floating-point axis labels
# Fuzzer stub requests multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() that are used as potential
# x/y/z axis label format strings and also a potential Window cell title.
# We therefore generate a buffer that, when split by the fuzzer into strings,
# yields a mix of valid printf float formats and some reasonable titles.
# Keep inputs valid: provide mostly correct printf formats, including width,
# precision, flags, and positional arguments, so different code paths are hit.

# We must implement generate(seed: int) -> bytes

_FLOAT_CONV = ["f", "F", "e", "E", "g", "G", "a", "A"]
_FLAGS = ["-", "+", " ", "#", "0"]

# Build a variety of valid float format strings, including positional and length variants
# Even though length like 'L' is allowed for long double, it's still a valid specifier.
def build_float_formats(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    fmts: List[str] = []

    # Some canonical simple formats
    fmts.extend([
        "%f", "%g", "%e", "%4.1f", "%06.2f", "%-8.3g", "%#.0f", "%+8.2f",
        "% .2e", "%#8.6g", "%0.1f", "%3f", "%8g", "%10.4e"
    ])

    # Randomly synthesize more
    for _ in range(20):
        parts = ["%"]
        # Optional positional argument like %1$4.1f
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 3)))
            parts.append("$")
        # Flags (unique, random order)
        flags = rng.sample(_FLAGS, rng.randint(0, len(_FLAGS)))
        parts.append("".join(flags))
        # Width
        if rng.random() < 0.85:
            # optional dynamic width using * or explicit int
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                # positional *
                if rng.random() < 0.5:
                    parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 3)))
                    parts.append("$*")
                else:
                    parts.append("*")
            else:
                parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 12)))
        # Precision
        if rng.random() < 0.9:
            parts.append(".")
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                # positional * for precision
                if rng.random() < 0.5:
                    parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 3)))
                    parts.append("$*")
                else:
                    parts.append("*")
            else:
                parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 8)))
        # Length modifier (mostly omit, occasionally L which is valid)
        parts.append("L" if rng.random() < 0.1 else "")
        # Conversion
        parts.append(rng.choice(_FLOAT_CONV))
        fmts.append("".join(parts))

    # Some with literal percent escaping (for titles combined with labels)
    fmts.append("%% literal %% and %4.1f")
    return fmts

# Build plausible window cell titles
_TITLES_BASE = [
    "ArrayFire Plot", "X vs Y", "Surface", "Histogram", "Scatter",
    "Temperature (°C)", "Signal Power (dB)", "Amplitude", "Phase", "Depth"
]

def build_titles(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    titles = list(_TITLES_BASE)
    # Add a few randomized titles with unicode and numbers
    for i in range(10):
        titles.append(f"Run {rng.randint(1,999)} - Series {rng.choice(['A','B','C','D'])}")
    # Include some empty or short titles (valid C strings, including empty)
    titles.extend(["", "X", "Y", "Z", "ΔX", "ΣY"])
    return titles

# The fuzzer will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() multiple times. We deliver a single
# bytes buffer; common fuzz harnesses split this buffer on NULs or newlines.
# We'll provide newline-separated strings so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can pull
# the next line. Include many valid format strings first, then some titles.

def assemble_buffer(strings: List[str], limit: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    data = ("\n".join(strings)).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > limit:
        data = data[:limit]
        # Ensure we end on a newline to keep clean separation
        if not data.endswith(b"\n"):
            data = data.rsplit(b"\n", 1)[0] + b"\n"
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    fmts = build_float_formats(rng)
    titles = build_titles(rng)

    # Mix of entries: prioritize valid format strings to maximize success,
    # but interleave with titles to serve as af_cell.title and also as fallback
    # if a format string is chosen from FUZZ_PARAM_STR for title field.
    entries: List[str] = []

    # Start with several guaranteed-good defaults often used by code
    entries.extend(["%4.1f", "%6.3f", "%+8.2f", "%g", "%e"]) 

    # Interleave random formats and titles
    rng.shuffle(fmts)
    rng.shuffle(titles)

    # Compose a sequence: majority formats, periodic titles
    for i, s in enumerate(fmts):
        entries.append(s)
        if i % 5 == 3 and titles:
            entries.append(titles.pop())

    # Append remaining titles at end
    entries.extend(titles[:15])

    # Make sure we also include a plain default like the stub's default "%4.1f"
    if "%4.1f" not in entries:
        entries.insert(0, "%4.1f")

    # Keep buffer size within 4096 bytes
    return assemble_buffer(entries, limit=4096)
